instructions: Knead the flour with the yeast, salt, a teaspoon of oil and 40 ml lukewarm water into a dough and leave to rise for 30 minutes.
Slice the onions into thin rings and cook slowly with the remaining oil and thyme over low heat for 25 minutes until soft and golden brown.
Preheat the oven to 220°C and roll the dough out thinly on a baking tray.
Spread the onions on top, add the anchovy fillets and olives and bake for 15 minutes.

title: Rice Congee with Chicken, Ginger and Spring Onions
instructions: Briefly wash the rice and bring to the boil with the stock, half of the ginger and the whole chicken fillet.
Simmer gently, covered, over low heat for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice has burst and turned porridge-like.
Remove the chicken and shred with two forks. Thinly slice the shiitake and cook in the congee for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken to the porridge, season with soy sauce and spoon into a deep bowl.
Top with the remaining ginger cut into fine strips, spring onion rings, coriander and sesame oil.

title: Tamagoyaki with Rice and Miso Soup
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions and keep warm.
Whisk the eggs with soy sauce and sugar. In a small, lightly oiled pan, cook thin layers of egg and roll each one up from back to front until you have a firm block.
Let the tamagoyaki rest briefly and slice.
Heat the stock, let the wakame and diced tofu steep in it for 3 minutes, remove from the heat and dissolve the miso in it (do not boil again).
Shape the rice into a ball and serve with the tamagoyaki and soup, sprinkling spring onions over the soup.

title: Masala Dosa with Potato Filling and Coconut Chutney
instructions: Soak the rice and urad dal separately in water for 6 hours, drain, blend until smooth with a little fresh water and leave to ferment somewhere warm overnight, then add salt.
Boil, peel and roughly mash the potatoes. Sweat the onion and ginger in 3 g oil with mustard seeds, turmeric and curry leaves and fold in the peas and potatoes.
Blend the coconut with chilli and a little water into a coarse chutney and salt it.
Brush a non-stick pan with the remaining oil, spread the batter thinly in a circle and cook over medium heat until crisp and golden brown.
Put the potato filling on the dosa, fold over and serve with the chutney.

title: Idli with Vegetable Sambar
ingredients: Sambar spice, mustard seeds, curry leaves
instructions: Soak the rice and urad dal separately, blend until smooth, mix and leave to ferment overnight, then add salt.
Fill the batter into greased idli moulds and steam for 12 minutes.
Cook the toor dal with water and turmeric until soft and stir until smooth.
Add the onion, carrot, okra and tomato and simmer with tamarind and sambar powder for 15 minutes. Briefly toast the mustard seeds and curry leaves and pour over.
Serve the idlis warm with the sambar.

title: Kaya Toast with Soft-Boiled Egg
instructions: Stir the egg, coconut milk and sugar in a bowl over a bain-marie constantly for 15 minutes until a thick, smooth cream (kaya) forms.
Let the kaya cool.
Boil an egg for 6 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve, or crack into a glass.
Toast the slices of bread until golden brown and spread with the kaya.
Eat the soft egg with a dash of soy sauce and pepper alongside the toast.

title: Dan Bing – Taiwanese Egg Pancake
instructions: Stir the flour, starch, water and a pinch of salt into a thin batter and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Brush a pan thinly with oil, spread the batter very thinly and cook over medium heat for 1–2 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, pour over the pancake with the spring onions and let it set.
Turn the pancake, finish cooking briefly and top with cucumber strips.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sambal, roll up from the sides and cut into pieces.

title: Poha with Peanuts and Peas
instructions: Briefly rinse the rice flakes in a sieve under cold water and leave to drain for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil and briefly toast the mustard seeds, curry leaves and peanuts in it.
Add the onion and diced potato and cook for 8–10 minutes, then stir in the peas.
Stir in the turmeric and salt, fold in the rice flakes and steam, covered, for 3 minutes.
Season with lime juice and coriander.

title: Moong Dal Chilla with Mint Yoghurt Chutney
instructions: Soak the moong dal for 3 hours, drain and blend with water, ginger and chilli into a smooth batter, then add salt.
Finely chop the onion, tomato and spinach and fold into the batter.
Lightly brush a non-stick pan with oil, spread a ladle of batter thinly and cook on both sides until golden brown.
Blend the herbs with the yoghurt and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Serve the chillas with the green chutney.

title: Champorado – Chocolate Sticky Rice Porridge with Coconut Milk
instructions: Bring the sticky rice to the boil with the water and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the cocoa and sugar and simmer for another 10 minutes until a thick, glossy porridge forms.
Add a splash of water if needed so nothing sticks.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with coconut milk and cold milk in a spiral pattern.

title: Pol Roti with Lentil Dhal
instructions: Knead the flour, desiccated coconut, chilli, half of the onion and salt with the water into a firm dough and leave to rest for 15 minutes.
Cook the lentils with water, turmeric, garlic and the remaining onion for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir in the coconut milk, add the curry leaves and reduce the dhal for 5 minutes until creamy, then salt it.
Divide the dough into two portions, press flat and cook on both sides in a dry pan until brown.
Serve the pol roti warm with the dhal.

title: Pho Bo – Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup
instructions: Toast the onion and ginger in a dry pot, add the stock, star anise and cinnamon stick and simmer gently for 20 minutes. Strain and season with fish sauce.
Soak the rice noodles according to the packet instructions, blanch briefly and put in a deep bowl.
Slice the beef wafer-thin and lay it on the noodles.
Pour the boiling hot stock over so that the meat cooks.
Serve with bean sprouts, herbs, chilli and lime wedges.

title: Air Fryer Prawn Lumpia with Sweet Chilli Dip
instructions: Roughly chop the prawns and mix with the carrot, white cabbage, spring onions, garlic and soy sauce.
Place a spoonful of filling on each wrapper, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and seal the edge with water.
Spray the lumpia with oil and cook in the air fryer at 190°C for 10–12 minutes until crisp and golden brown, turning once.
Bring the sambal to the boil with sugar, vinegar and 2 tbsp water until the dip is slightly thick.
Serve the lumpia hot with the dip.

title: Cá Kho Tộ – Caramelised Trout with Rice
instructions: Cook the sugar with 1 tbsp water in a small saucepan into a golden-brown caramel.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in oil for 2 minutes and add the fish sauce, water and chilli.
Cut the trout fillet into pieces, place in the sauce and braise gently, covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove the lid and reduce the sauce for 5 minutes into a glossy syrup.
Serve with cooked rice, cucumber and tomato slices and spring onions.

title: Tom Kha Gai – Thai Coconut Soup with Chicken
instructions: Bring the stock to the boil with the lemongrass and ginger slices and leave to infuse for 5 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, add the chicken in thin strips and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and tomato pieces and cook for 4 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice and chilli (do not boil hard again).
Serve with coriander and separately cooked rice; don't eat the lemongrass and ginger slices.

title: Som Tam – Papaya Salad with Prawns and Sticky Rice
instructions: Soak the sticky rice for 2 hours and steam for 20 minutes.
Cook the prawns in boiling water for 2–3 minutes until pink, then cool in cold water.
Pound the garlic and chilli in a mortar, stir in the sugar, lime juice and fish sauce and lightly bruise the beans and tomatoes.
Add the papaya strips and pound briefly so they absorb the flavour.
Top with the prawns and peanuts and serve with the sticky rice.

title: Green Thai Curry with Tofu and Thai Aubergine
ingredients: Green curry paste (vegan, without shrimp paste)
instructions: Cook the rice. Pat the tofu dry, dice and fry in 2 g oil until crisp, then remove.
Toast the curry paste in the remaining oil for 1 minute and pour in the coconut milk and water.
Simmer the aubergine and bamboo shoots for 8 minutes, add the pepper and cook for 3 minutes.
Return the tofu to the sauce and season with soy sauce and sugar.
Sprinkle with Thai basil and serve with the rice.

title: Mango Sticky Rice
instructions: Soak the sticky rice for 3 hours, drain and steam for 20 minutes.
Warm the coconut milk with the sugar and a pinch of salt; do not boil.
Mix the hot rice with two-thirds of the coconut milk and leave to steep, covered, for 10 minutes.
Peel the mango and cut into a fan.
Arrange the rice with the mango, drizzle over the remaining coconut milk and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Laksa with Prawns, Tofu and Rice Noodles
instructions: Toast the curry paste with the lemongrass and ginger in a pot without fat for 1 minute.
Add the stock and coconut milk and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Cook the rice noodles according to the packet instructions and put in a deep bowl.
Add the prawns and diced tofu to the broth and let them steep for 3 minutes.
Pour the soup over the noodles and serve with sprouts, cucumber, herbs and lime juice.

title: Nasi Goreng with Tempeh and Vegetables
ingredients: Jasmine rice (uncooked weight, cooked the day before)
instructions: Cook the rice and ideally let it cool overnight so it stays fluffy and separate.
Finely dice the tempeh, fry in half of the oil in a hot wok until crisp and remove.
Toss the garlic, carrot, cabbage and peas for 3 minutes, add the rice and fry over high heat.
Season with soy sauce and sambal and fold in the tempeh.
Serve with cucumber slices and a little crispy fried garlic in place of fried onions.

title: Gado-Gado with Peanut Sauce
instructions: Cook the potatoes, let them cool and slice. Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes.
Blanch the beans, cabbage and sprouts one after another for 2–3 minutes and cool in cold water.
Dice the tofu and fry in a pan with little fat until golden brown.
Stir the peanut butter, coconut milk, lime juice, soy sauce, garlic and chilli in a saucepan until smooth and warm briefly.
Arrange the vegetables, potatoes, tofu, cucumber and egg and coat with the sauce.

title: Air Fryer Chicken Satay with Cucumber Salad
instructions: Cut the chicken into strips and marinate with the spices, garlic, soy sauce and half of the coconut milk for 20 minutes.
Thread onto wooden skewers and cook in the air fryer at 190°C for 10–12 minutes, turning once.
Warm the peanut butter with the remaining coconut milk and a little water until a smooth sauce forms.
Thinly slice the cucumber and onion and dress with vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Serve the skewers with peanut sauce, cucumber salad and cooked rice.

title: Chicken Rendang with Coconut and Rice
instructions: Blend the onion, garlic, ginger and chilli with a little water into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil for 3 minutes and add the lemongrass, cumin and cinnamon.
Add the chicken pieces and coconut milk, braise covered for 25 minutes and then reduce uncovered into a dark, thick sauce.
Season with lime juice, palm sugar and salt. Cook the rice and steam the pak choi for 3 minutes.
Serve the chicken with rice and pak choi.

title: Sinigang na Hipon – Sour Prawn Soup
instructions: Bring the water to the boil with the onion, tomato and diced potato and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the tamarind, radish slices and okra and simmer for 6 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and add the chilli.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink.
Fold in the spinach, let it wilt and serve immediately.

title: Pancit Bihon – Filipino Rice Noodles with Vegetables
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Fry the prawns in oil for 2 minutes and remove.
Fry the garlic, onion, carrot, beans and cabbage for 4 minutes.
Add the stock and soy sauce, add the noodles and toss for 3–4 minutes until the liquid has been absorbed.
Fold in the prawns and serve with lime.

title: Air Fryer Chicken Inasal with Rice and Cucumber Tomato Salad
instructions: Finely chop the lemongrass and stir with the lime juice, vinegar, garlic, ginger and half of the oil.
Add the chicken thighs and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Cook in the air fryer at 190°C for 18–20 minutes, turning once and brushing with marinade.
Cook the rice. Dice the tomato and cucumber and dress with a little lime juice and salt.
Serve the chicken with rice and salad.

title: Bibimbap with Vegetables and Fried Egg
instructions: Cook the rice. Fry the minced beef with soy sauce and garlic powder in a dry pan until crumbly.
Blanch the spinach and sprouts for 1 minute each, squeeze out and marinate with a little sesame oil.
Briefly fry the carrot, courgette and shiitake separately in strips.
Fry an egg in the pan.
Arrange the rice in a deep bowl with the vegetables, mince and egg, add gochujang and sesame seeds and mix everything together before eating.

title: Kung Pao Prawns with Pepper and Peanuts
instructions: Cook the rice. Mix the prawns with starch and a little soy sauce.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and 3 tbsp water into a sauce.
Fry the chilli, garlic and ginger in oil in a hot wok for 30 seconds, fry the prawns with them for 2 minutes and remove.
Stir-fry the pepper and courgette over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the prawns and sauce, reduce for 1 minute, fold in the peanuts and serve with rice.

title: Dim Sum–Style Steamed Prawn Dumplings
instructions: Roughly chop the prawns and mix with the bamboo shoots, spring onions, ginger, sesame oil and a little soy sauce.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, moisten the edges and pleat closed into half-moons.
Steam the dumplings in a bamboo basket on baking paper for 8–10 minutes.
Thinly slice the cucumber and carrot and briefly marinate with some of the vinegar.
Serve the remaining soy sauce mixed with vinegar as a dip with the dumplings.

title: Cantonese Steamed Sea Bream with Ginger and Spring Onions
instructions: Cook the rice. Cut the ginger and spring onions into fine strips.
Place the sea bream fillets on a plate, top with half of the ginger strips and steam for 7–8 minutes.
Steam the pak choi alongside for 3 minutes.
Pour off the cooking liquid. Top the fish with the remaining ginger and spring onions and drizzle with soy sauce.
Heat the rapeseed oil and sesame oil until hot and pour over the ginger and onions; serve with rice and coriander.

title: Cold Sichuan Sesame Noodles with Cucumber and Edamame
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, rinse under cold water and drain.
Boil the edamame for 3 minutes and let them cool.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into fine strips.
Stir the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sambal, garlic and 2 tbsp water into a smooth sauce.
Mix everything together and sprinkle with spring onions.

title: Yu Xiang Aubergine with Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Cut the aubergine into batons, salt and leave for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Fry the aubergine in 6 g oil in a wok over high heat for 8 minutes until soft and browned, then remove.
Briefly toast the garlic, ginger and doubanjiang in the remaining oil.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, a little water and the starch slurry and bring to the boil.
Return the aubergine to the wok, toss and serve with spring onions and rice.

title: Napa Cabbage and Tofu Soup with Glass Noodles and Shiitake
instructions: Bring the stock to the boil with the ginger slices and soy sauce.
Add the sliced shiitake and the Chinese cabbage in strips and simmer for 6 minutes.
Dice the tofu and let it steep in the soup for 3 minutes.
Soak the glass noodles in warm water and add them to the soup just before serving.
Season with sesame oil and spring onions.

title: Saba Shioyaki – Grilled Mackerel with Rice and Daikon
instructions: Cook the rice. Season the mackerel fillet with salt, leave for 10 minutes and pat dry.
Cook the fish skin side up under the oven grill or skin side down in a griddle pan for 4 minutes until crisp, turn and finish cooking for 3 minutes.
Finely grate the radish and squeeze lightly. Thinly slice the cucumber and marinate with vinegar, wakame and sesame seeds.
Arrange the fish with a small mound of radish, a dash of soy sauce and lemon.
Serve with rice and cucumber salad.

title: Cold Soba with Sesame Dip, Cucumber and Tofu
instructions: Cook the soba noodles according to the packet instructions, rinse in ice-cold water and drain well.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into fine batons and the smoked tofu into strips.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, 80 ml cold water and ground sesame seeds into a dip.
Arrange the noodles with the vegetables and tofu on a plate and sprinkle with nori strips.
Add the spring onions to the dip and dunk the noodles as you eat.

title: Gyudon – Japanese Beef Rice Bowl with Onions
instructions: Cook the rice and put it in a deep bowl.
Bring the stock to the boil in a pan with the soy sauce, sugar and ginger.
Add the onion rings and simmer for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the beef slices and cook for 2–3 minutes until just done; add the edamame.
Spoon the meat and onions with a little of the liquid over the rice and sprinkle with spring onions.

title: Salmon Onigiri with Edamame Miso Soup
instructions: Cook the rice and let it cool slightly.
Cook the salmon in a pan or in the oven and flake it with a fork.
With wet hands, shape the rice into triangles, fill the centre with salmon and wrap with nori. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Heat the stock, let the edamame steep for 3 minutes, remove the pot from the heat and stir in the miso.
Serve the onigiri with the soup and spring onions.

title: Japchae – Korean Glass Noodles with Beef and Vegetables
instructions: Boil the glass noodles for 7 minutes, drain, rinse briefly in cold water and toss with a little sesame oil and soy sauce.
Marinate the beef strips with a little soy sauce, garlic and sugar.
Blanch the spinach for 1 minute and squeeze out. Fry the onion, carrot, pepper and shiitake one after another in a little oil for 2–3 minutes.
Cook the beef through in the hot pan for 2 minutes.
Toss everything with the noodles, season with the remaining soy sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Chana Masala with Chapati
instructions: Fry the onion in oil for 8 minutes until golden brown, then add the garlic and ginger.
Toast the spices for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and reduce for 8 minutes.
Add the chickpeas with 100 ml water and simmer for 12 minutes, mashing some of the chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Knead the flour with water and salt into a dough, divide into 2 portions, roll out thinly and cook on both sides in a hot dry pan.
Serve the chana masala with fresh coriander and chapati.

title: Palak Paneer with Basmati Rice
instructions: Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, cool in cold water, squeeze out and purée finely.
Sweat the onion in oil until translucent, add the garlic, ginger and spices and reduce the tomato for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach purée, simmer for 5 minutes and stir in the yoghurt.
Dice the paneer, fry in a non-stick pan without fat until golden brown and add to the sauce.
Cook the rice and serve with the palak paneer.

title: Dal Bhat Tarkari – Nepali Lentils and Rice with Vegetables
instructions: Cook the dal with water, turmeric and ginger for 25 minutes until soft, then add salt.
Cook the rice. Cut the potato and cauliflower into pieces.
Fry the onion and garlic in 4 g oil with cumin, add the potatoes, cauliflower and tomato and cook with a splash of water for 15 minutes (tarkari).
Sauté the spinach with a little salt and the remaining oil in a pan for 3 minutes (saag).
Arrange the rice, dal, tarkari and spinach on a plate.

title: Sri Lankan Mackerel Curry with Coconut and Rice
ingredients: Curry powder, turmeric, cinnamon, curry leaves
instructions: Sweat the onion, garlic and ginger in oil and briefly toast the spices and curry leaves.
Add the tomato, chilli, tamarind and coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes.
Cut the mackerel into pieces and cook in the sauce, covered, for 7 minutes.
Cook the rice and blanch the beans for 4 minutes.
Serve the curry with rice and beans.

title: Kheer – Indian Rice Pudding with Pistachios and Cardamom
instructions: Briefly wash the rice and soak in water for 20 minutes.
Bring the milk to the boil, add the rice and cardamom and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often.
Add the sugar and raisins and cook for another 5 minutes until the pudding is creamy.
Spoon into bowls warm or chilled and sprinkle with chopped pistachios.

title: Chilaquiles Rojos with Black Beans
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (fan). Cut the tortillas into triangles, brush with rapeseed oil and bake for 8–10 minutes until crisp.
Reduce the passata with chilli, salt and pepper in a pan for 5 minutes.
Toss the tortilla chips in the sauce until slightly soft but still with some bite.
Briefly warm the beans and scatter on top along with the cheese.
Serve with onion rings, diced avocado and coriander.

title: Aguachile de Camarones with Cucumber and Avocado
instructions: Blanch the prawns in boiling water for 1 minute, cool in cold water and halve lengthways.
Blend the lime juice, chilli, coriander and a pinch of salt into a green marinade.
Let the prawns steep in the marinade with cucumber slices and thin onion rings for 10 minutes.
Arrange on a plate, place avocado slices alongside and serve with the tostadas.

title: Pescado a la Veracruzana with Cod and Olives
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Fry the onion and pepper in olive oil, add the diced tomatoes, jalapeño, olives and capers and reduce for 10 minutes.
Salt the cod, drizzle with lime juice and place in the sauce.
Cook gently, covered, for 8–10 minutes until the fish is done.
Serve with the rice.

title: Peruvian Ceviche with Sweet Potato and Corn
instructions: Cut the sea bream into 2 cm cubes and salt.
Slice the onion into thin rings and rinse briefly in cold water.
Mix the fish with lime juice, chilli, onion and coriander and marinate for 5 minutes until the outside of the flesh turns white.
Slice the sweet potato and arrange on the plate with the corn.
Serve the ceviche with its juice (leche de tigre) alongside and eat immediately.

title: Lomo Saltado with Rice
instructions: Cut the potatoes into batons, toss with half of the oil and bake in the oven at 220°C for 25 minutes until crisp. Cook the rice in the meantime.
Cut the steak into strips and sear in a very hot pan or wok for 2 minutes.
Add the onion wedges, tomato wedges and chilli and fry for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with soy sauce and a splash of vinegar.
Fold in the potato batons, sprinkle with coriander and serve with the rice.

title: Moqueca de Camarão with Coconut Milk and Rice
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Cut the onion, pepper and tomatoes into strips and fry in the olive oil for 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the prawns with lime juice and salt and let them cook through for 4 minutes.
Sprinkle with plenty of coriander and serve with the rice.

title: Pão de Queijo with Papaya
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (fan).
Briefly bring the milk and rapeseed oil to the boil, pour over the tapioca starch, stir and let it cool a little.
Knead in the egg and grated cheese until a sticky dough forms.
With damp hands, shape into small balls and bake for 20 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve warm with papaya pieces.

title: Arepas with Black Beans, Avocado and Cheese
instructions: Knead the cornmeal with 100 ml warm water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Shape two flat discs and fry in a pan with a little oil for 5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Bake in the oven at 180°C for another 10 minutes until they sound hollow.
Warm the beans with salt and cumin.
Slice the arepas open and fill with beans, cheese, avocado and diced tomato.

title: Ajiaco Bogotano (Colombian Chicken Soup)
instructions: Boil the onion and half of the potatoes in 600 ml salted water for 15 minutes and roughly mash; this makes the soup thick and creamy.
Add the chicken breast and the remaining diced potatoes and cook for 20 minutes.
Remove the chicken, shred and return to the soup.
Add the corn and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve in bowls with diced avocado, capers, coriander and a dollop of yoghurt.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken with Rice, Beans and Pineapple Salsa
instructions: Rub the chicken thighs with jerk seasoning, salt and a little lime juice and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Bake in the oven at 200°C for 30–35 minutes until the skinless surface is dark and caramelised.
Cook the rice with the kidney beans, water and a splash of coconut milk.
Finely dice the pineapple and red onion and mix with lime juice and coriander to make the salsa.
Arrange everything together.

title: Moros y Cristianos with Baked Plantain
instructions: Slice the plantain, brush with some of the oil and bake in the oven at 200°C for 20 minutes until caramelised.
Sweat the onion and pepper in olive oil until soft, then add the spices.
Stir in the rice and beans with 120 ml water and cook, covered, for 15 minutes until the rice is tender.
Season with salt and serve with the plantain.

title: Air Fryer Plátanos Maduros with Coconut Yoghurt
instructions: Peel the plantain and cut diagonally into 1 cm thick slices.
Toss with rapeseed oil and cinnamon.
Cook in the air fryer at 190°C for 10–12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown and caramelised.
Stir the yoghurt with honey and lime zest.
Serve the plantain with the yoghurt and coconut flakes.

title: Air Fryer Southern Fried Chicken with Coleslaw
instructions: Marinate the chicken with 40 g yoghurt, salt, paprika and garlic powder for at least 30 minutes.
Mix the panko with flour and spices, coat the chicken in it and spray or drizzle with rapeseed oil.
Cook in the air fryer at 190°C for 22–25 minutes, turning halfway.
Mix the cabbage and carrot with the remaining yoghurt, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper to make the coleslaw.
Serve the chicken with the coleslaw.

title: Turkey Meatloaf with Mashed Potatoes and Green Beans
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Knead the turkey mince with panko, egg, finely diced onion, mustard, salt and pepper and shape into a small loaf.
Brush with tomato purée and bake for 35 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and mash with milk. Boil the beans for 6 minutes and toss in rapeseed oil.
Slice the meatloaf and serve with the mash and beans.

title: Sweet Potato with Black Beans and Corn Salsa
instructions: Wash the sweet potatoes, prick with a fork and bake in the oven at 200°C for 40–45 minutes.
Warm the beans with cumin and salt.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, corn, lime juice and coriander to make the salsa.
Slit the sweet potatoes lengthways and fill with beans and salsa.
Top with diced avocado and a dollop of yoghurt.

title: Steel-Cut Oatmeal with Maple Syrup, Pecans and Apple
instructions: Bring the oats to the boil with the milk, 100 ml water and cinnamon and simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Dice the apple and soften in a small pan with a little cinnamon for 3 minutes.
Roughly chop the pecans and briefly toast in a dry pan.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the apple, nuts and maple syrup.

title: Waldorf Salad with Smoked Trout
instructions: Finely grate the celeriac and mix with lemon juice so it stays pale.
Dice the apple with the skin on and mix with the celeriac.
Stir the yoghurt with mustard, salt and pepper and fold in.
Arrange on salad leaves, sprinkle with chopped walnuts and lay the trout pieces on top.
Serve with the bread.

title: Air Fryer Maple Salmon with Wild Rice and Broccoli
instructions: Cook the wild rice according to the packet instructions for 35–40 minutes.
Stir together the maple syrup, mustard and soy sauce and brush over the salmon.
Cook in the air fryer at 180°C for 8–10 minutes.
Divide the broccoli into florets and steam for 4 minutes.
Arrange the salmon with the wild rice and broccoli.

title: Swedish Köttbullar with Mashed Potatoes and Cucumber Salad
instructions: Soak the panko in milk and knead with the mince, egg, grated onion, allspice, salt and pepper.
Shape into small balls and fry all over in rapeseed oil over medium heat for 8–10 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and mash with the milk.
Slice the cucumber wafer-thin and marinate with vinegar, salt and dill for 10 minutes.
Serve the köttbullar with the mash, lingonberries and cucumber salad.

title: Gravlax with Mustard Dill Sauce and Crispbread
instructions: Stir the mustard with yoghurt, honey, lemon juice and plenty of chopped dill until smooth.
Slice the cucumber thinly.
Cut the salmon into thin slices.
Top the crispbread with cucumber and salmon and spoon the sauce over.

title: Karelian Pasties with Rice Porridge and Egg Butter
instructions: Cook the pudding rice with the milk and a little salt for 25 minutes into a thick porridge and let it cool.
Knead the rye flour, wheat flour, 60 ml water and salt into a firm dough and roll out very thinly into two oval rounds.
Place the rice porridge in the middle and fold in the edges in a wavy pattern.
Bake at 250°C for 12–15 minutes until the edges are dark.
Chop the egg, mix with soft butter and spread on the warm pasties.

title: Smørrebrød with Matjes Herring, Beetroot and Apple
instructions: Stir the yoghurt with mustard and dill and spread on the slices of rye bread.
Cut the beetroot and apple into thin slices.
Lay the matjes fillets on the bread and top with beetroot and apple.
Garnish with red onion rings and dill.

title: Light Rødgrød med Fløde (Danish Red Berry Pudding)
instructions: Simmer the berries gently with the sugar and 50 ml water for 5 minutes.
Mix the starch with 2 tbsp cold water, stir into the berries and boil for 1 minute.
Pour into a glass and let it cool.
Stir the yoghurt with vanilla, spoon over and sprinkle with slivered almonds.

title: Barszcz Czerwony (Polish Beetroot Soup) with Potatoes and Egg
instructions: Dice the onion, carrot and beetroot and boil in 600 ml water for 15 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, marjoram and a splash of vinegar.
Boil the potatoes separately.
Ladle the soup into bowls and serve with the halved egg, yoghurt and dill.
Serve the potatoes and rye bread alongside.

title: Syrniki (Russian Quark Pancakes) with Berries
instructions: Drain the quark well and stir with the egg, flour, sugar, vanilla and a pinch of salt into a firm dough.
With floured hands, shape 5–6 small flat cakes.
Fry in a non-stick pan with rapeseed oil over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve with berries and yoghurt.

title: Buckwheat with Mushrooms and Onions (Grechka)
instructions: Briefly toast the buckwheat in a dry pan, bring to the boil with twice the amount of salted water and leave to swell, covered, for 15 minutes.
Dice the onion and fry in rapeseed oil until golden brown.
Add the sliced mushrooms and fry vigorously for 8 minutes until they take on colour.
Season with salt and pepper and mix with the buckwheat.
Serve with yoghurt, dill and pickled gherkin.

title: Lobio with Walnuts and Mchadi (Georgia)
instructions: Fry the onion in rapeseed oil until golden brown.
Simmer the beans with half of the onion and a little water for 10 minutes and roughly mash.
Finely pound the walnuts with garlic, coriander, fenugreek and a splash of vinegar and stir in.
Knead the cornmeal with warm water and salt into a dough, shape into two flatbreads and cook in a dry pan for 5 minutes per side.
Serve the lobio with pomegranate seeds and the mchadi flatbreads.

title: Chakhokhbili (Georgian Chicken and Tomato Stew) with Potatoes
instructions: Fry the chicken all over in rapeseed oil for 8 minutes.
Add the onion rings and pepper and fry for 5 minutes.
Dice the tomatoes, add and braise, covered, over low heat for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes.
Season with coriander, basil and garlic and serve with the potatoes.

title: Lamb Ćevapčići with Ajvar and Pepper Salad
instructions: Knead the lamb and beef mince vigorously with salt, pepper, garlic, a pinch of baking powder and a splash of cold water for 5 minutes and chill for 1 hour.
Shape into finger-thick rolls.
Grill all over in a hot griddle pan for 10 minutes.
Dice the pepper and cucumber and arrange as a salad with onion rings.
Serve with flatbread and ajvar.

title: Moules Marinières (Mussels) with Baguette and Chips
instructions: Cut the potatoes into batons, toss with half of the oil and bake at 220°C for 25 minutes until crisp.
Finely dice the onion and celery and sweat in the remaining oil until translucent.
Add the stock and lemon juice, bring to the boil, add the cleaned mussels and steam, covered, for 5–6 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay closed.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with baguette and chips.

title: Cotriade Bretonne (Breton Fish Stew with Mackerel)
instructions: Sweat the onion and leek in olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the potato slices, passata, bay leaf, thyme and 400 ml water and boil for 15 minutes.
Cut the pollock and mackerel into large pieces and add to the pot.
Poach gently, covered, for 8 minutes.
Serve with parsley and a splash of vinegar.

title: Cherry Clafoutis
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (fan) and grease a small baking dish with butter.
Spread the cherries in the dish.
Whisk the egg with the flour, milk, honey, vanilla and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Pour the batter over the cherries and bake for 30–35 minutes until golden brown and set.
Serve lukewarm.

title: Irish Stew with Lamb
instructions: Dice the lamb and briefly sear all over in rapeseed oil.
Cut the onion, carrot and leek into large pieces and add.
Dice the potatoes, add with the stock and thyme and bring everything to the boil.
Braise gently, covered, for 50 minutes until the meat is tender.
Serve sprinkled with parsley.

title: Cullen Skink (Scottish Smoked Fish Soup)
instructions: Sweat the onion and leek in butter until soft.
Add the diced potatoes and 250 ml water and cook for 12 minutes.
Place the haddock in the soup and poach for 6 minutes, then remove the fish and flake it.
Mash some of the potatoes, add the milk and warm briefly.
Return the fish, season and serve with chives.

title: Sardinhas Assadas with Tomato and Pepper Salad
instructions: Rub the sardines with coarse salt and leave for 10 minutes.
Roast the peppers in the oven at 230°C for 15 minutes, peel and cut into strips.
Mix the tomatoes, onion and peppers with olive oil, vinegar and salt to make the salad.
Grill the sardines in a griddle pan or under the oven grill for 3–4 minutes per side.
Serve with jacket-boiled potatoes, salad and lemon.

title: Polvo à Lagareiro: Octopus with Roast Potatoes and Kale
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Boil the potatoes in their skins, press lightly flat ("a murro") and sprinkle with salt.
Place the octopus on a baking tray with the potatoes, onion wedges and garlic cloves, drizzle with olive oil and roast for 20 minutes.
Cook the kale in a pan with a little garlic for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with the kale.

title: Jollof Rice with Grilled Tilapia
instructions: Finely blend the pepper, onion, chilli and tomatoes.
Reduce the paste in rapeseed oil over high heat for 10 minutes until it darkens.
Stir in the rice and 100 ml water and cook, covered, for 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rub the tilapia with spices and grill or fry for 4 minutes per side.
Serve the jollof rice with the fish.

title: Misir Wot with Injera (Ethiopia)
instructions: Chop the onions very finely and sweat in a pot without fat for 10 minutes, then add the oil.
Toast the tomato purée, berbere, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the red lentils and 300 ml water and cook for 20 minutes, stirring, into a thick stew.
Season with salt.
Serve on an injera with more injera pieces for dipping.

title: Bobotie with Yellow Rice (South Africa)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Soak the bread in half of the milk and squeeze out.
Fry the onion in rapeseed oil, add the mince, curry powder and turmeric and fry until crumbly.
Stir in the grated apple, raisins, almonds, bread, salt and pepper and press into a dish.
Whisk the egg with the remaining milk, pour over the mince, lay a bay leaf on top and bake for 25 minutes.
Cook the rice with turmeric and serve alongside.

title: Pap with Chakalaka (South Africa)
instructions: Fry the onion in rapeseed oil and add the curry powder and chilli.
Grate the carrot, dice the pepper and tomatoes and cook down with the beans for 15 minutes to make chakalaka.
Stir the maize meal into 250 ml boiling salted water and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, into a firm porridge.
Turn the pap out onto plates and arrange the chakalaka alongside.

title: Mafé: Senegalese Peanut Stew with Sweet Potato
instructions: Fry the onion in rapeseed oil and add the tomato purée, chilli, ginger and garlic.
Dice the sweet potato, add with 400 ml water and boil for 10 minutes.
Stir the peanut butter into a little hot stock until smooth and stir it in.
Add the cabbage and chickpeas and simmer gently for 15 minutes until everything is tender.
Season with salt and serve hot.

title: Wild Garlic Soup with Potatoes and Rye Croutons
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in half of the rapeseed oil until translucent.
Dice the potatoes, add and pour in the stock. Cook for 15 minutes until soft.
Dice the rye bread and toast in the remaining oil in a pan until crisp.
Roughly chop the wild garlic, add to the soup with the milk and blend everything until smooth. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Serve the soup in deep plates with the croutons.

title: Wild Garlic Cream Cheese Spread on Rye Bread with Radishes
instructions: Finely chop the wild garlic and stir with the cream cheese, salt and pepper until creamy.
Spread the rye bread thinly with butter.
Spread the cream cheese thickly on top.
Slice the radishes, arrange on the bread and sprinkle with a little coarse salt.

title: Pike-Perch on Braised Leeks with Parsley Potatoes
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cook in salted water for 18 minutes and toss with chopped parsley.
Cut the leek into rings and sauté in the rapeseed oil for 6 minutes. Stir in the soured cream and season.
Season the pike-perch with salt and pepper and fry skin side down in butter for 4 minutes until crisp, turn briefly and leave for 1 minute.
Divide the leeks between plates, place the pike-perch on top and serve with the potatoes and lemon wedges.

title: Trout Meunière with Green Beans and Boiled Potatoes
instructions: Cook the potatoes in salted water for 18 minutes. Trim the beans and cook in salted water for 8 minutes until tender but firm.
Season the trout fillets with lemon juice, salt and pepper and dust lightly in flour.
Heat half of the butter and fry the fillets for 3 minutes per side until golden brown, then remove.
Let the remaining butter foam in the pan, toast the almonds in it and pour over the fish.
Arrange with the potatoes, beans and parsley.

title: Matjes Herring in Creamy Apple Sauce with Jacket Potatoes
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes.
Finely dice the apple, onion and gherkin and stir with the yoghurt, pepper and dill.
Pat the matjes fillets dry and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Pour the sauce over the herring and serve with the hot jacket potatoes.

title: Smoked Mackerel on Rye Bread with Beetroot and Apple Salad
instructions: Coarsely grate the beetroot and apple.
Stir the yoghurt with horseradish, lemon juice and salt and mix with the beetroot and apple.
Remove any bones from the mackerel fillet and break into pieces.
Top the rye bread with the salad and mackerel, or arrange everything side by side.

title: Baked Herring with Mustard Crust on Root Vegetables
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (conventional). Cut the parsnip, carrot and celeriac into batons, toss with rapeseed oil, salt and pepper and roast for 25 minutes.
Pat the herring fillets dry, salt and brush with mustard.
Press the oats onto the mustard and place the fillets on the vegetables.
Bake for another 10–12 minutes until the crust is golden brown. Serve with parsley.

title: Potato Soup with Frankfurters
instructions: Cut the potatoes, carrot and celeriac into small cubes and the leek into rings.
Briefly sweat the vegetables in the rapeseed oil, pour in the stock and simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend a quarter of the soup with a stick blender to thicken it and stir back in.
Season with marjoram, salt and pepper.
Slice the frankfurters, warm in the soup and serve with parsley.

title: Swede Stew with White Beans
instructions: Peel the swede, potatoes, carrot and celeriac and cut into 2 cm cubes. Dice the onion.
Sweat the onion in the rapeseed oil until translucent and briefly fry the vegetables.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 25 minutes until everything is soft.
Add the beans and mash some of the vegetable pieces to thicken the stew.
Season with marjoram, salt and pepper and serve with parsley.

title: Kale with Potatoes and Turkey Bratwurst
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the rapeseed oil. Roughly tear the kale and add.
Pour in the stock, add the diced potatoes and braise, covered, for 25 minutes.
Stir in the oats (they thicken the kale, as is done in northern Germany) and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Fry the bratwurst in a pan until brown all over.
Season the kale with mustard, salt and pepper and serve with the bratwurst.

title: Savoy Cabbage Rolls with Mince Filling and Potatoes
instructions: Blanch the savoy cabbage leaves in salted water for 2 minutes and drain.
Knead the mince with diced onion, oats, egg, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Place the filling on the leaves, roll up and secure with kitchen string or cocktail sticks.
Brown the rolls all over in the rapeseed oil, add the tomato purée and stock and braise for 25 minutes.
Serve with boiled potatoes and spoon the sauce over.

title: Creamy Mushrooms (Rahmschwammerl) with Polenta
instructions: Stir the polenta into 200 ml boiling salted stock and leave to swell over low heat for 10 minutes.
Clean and slice the mushrooms. Dice the onion.
Sweat the onion in the rapeseed oil, add the mushrooms and fry vigorously for 8 minutes until the liquid has evaporated.
Deglaze with the stock, stir in the soured cream and reduce briefly. Season with salt, pepper and caraway.
Spoon the polenta onto plates and arrange the mushrooms on top with parsley.

title: Stuffed Hokkaido Squash with Spelt, Chestnuts and Apple
instructions: Cook the spelt according to the packet instructions for 30–35 minutes until soft. Preheat the oven to 200°C (conventional).
Halve and deseed the squash and pre-bake for 15 minutes.
Dice the onion and apple, fry in the rapeseed oil and mix with the spelt, chopped chestnuts, thyme, salt and pepper.
Spoon the filling into the squash halves and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.
Bake for another 20 minutes until the squash is soft.

title: Styrian Runner Bean Salad with Pumpkin Seed Oil
instructions: Rinse and drain the beans.
Cut the onion into thin rings and dice the tomato.
Mix the beans with the onion, tomato, cider vinegar, salt and pepper and leave to marinate for 10 minutes.
Arrange on plates, drizzle with dark green pumpkin seed oil and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds.
Serve with rye bread.

title: Krautfleckerl (Austrian Cabbage Pasta)
instructions: Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente.
Finely shred the white cabbage and dice the onion.
Lightly caramelise the sugar in the rapeseed oil, add the onion and cabbage and braise over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden brown.
Season with caraway, paprika, salt and pepper.
Mix the pasta into the cabbage and serve hot.

title: Tyrolean Gröstl with Fried Egg
instructions: Slice the cooked potatoes. Cut the beef into small cubes and the onion into rings.
Sear the meat in half of the oil in a large pan and remove.
Fry the potatoes in the remaining oil for 8–10 minutes until crisp, add the onion and brown it too.
Return the meat to the pan and season with marjoram, salt and pepper.
Fry an egg, place on top of the gröstl and serve with chives and a gherkin.

title: Light Swiss Alpine Macaroni with Apple Sauce
instructions: Dice the potatoes and boil together with the pasta in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Cut the onion into thin rings and fry in the rapeseed oil over medium heat until golden brown.
Return the pasta and potatoes to the pot with the milk and mountain cheese and stir until melted.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Arrange on plates with the fried onions and serve the apple sauce separately.

title: Zurich-Style Sliced Veal with Potato Rösti
instructions: Coarsely grate the potatoes, squeeze out, salt and fry in a non-stick pan with half of the oil as a flat rösti for 8 minutes per side until golden brown.
Cut the veal into thin strips, sear in the remaining oil and remove.
Fry the onion and mushrooms until they take on colour.
Return the meat, stir in the soured cream and warm for 2 minutes. Season with salt, pepper and parsley.
Arrange the veal next to the rösti.

title: Chicken Fricassée with Asparagus and Rice
instructions: Poach the chicken in the stock for 12 minutes, remove and dice. Keep the stock. Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Peel the asparagus and cut into pieces; quarter the mushrooms. Fry both in the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes.
Dust with the flour, deglaze with the stock and milk and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, into a creamy sauce.
Add the chicken and peas and leave for 3 minutes. Season with lemon juice, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Serve with the rice.

title: Venison Goulash with Mushrooms and Mashed Potatoes
instructions: Pat the venison dry and sear vigorously in the rapeseed oil in batches, then remove.
Fry the onions, briefly toast the tomato purée, return the meat and pour in the stock. Add the juniper and bay leaf.
Braise gently for 45 minutes, stirring in the mushrooms and lingonberries for the last 10 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and mash with the warm milk.
Serve the goulash with the mash.

title: Light Obazda with Pretzel and Radishes
instructions: Mash the Camembert with a fork and stir with the cream cheese, paprika, caraway, salt and pepper until creamy.
Dice the onion very finely and fold in.
Using a spoon, shape the obazda into a dome on a board.
Garnish with onion rings and radishes and serve with the pretzel.

title: Liptauer Spread on Rye Bread with Cucumber and Pepper
ingredients: Sweet paprika, caraway, capers, mustard, salt
instructions: Stir the quark with soft butter, paprika, caraway, capers, mustard and salt until smooth.
Dice the onion very finely and fold in.
Leave the Liptauer to infuse for at least 10 minutes.
Spread the rye bread thickly and top with cucumber and pepper strips.

title: Hessian Hand Cheese "with Music" (Onion Vinaigrette) and Rye Bread
instructions: Cut the onion into thin rings.
Stir together the vinegar, rapeseed oil, caraway, salt and pepper and marinate the onions in it for 10 minutes.
Place the cheese on a plate and pour over the marinade and onions.
Leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes and serve with rye bread.

title: Oven-Baked Potato Pancakes with Apple Sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C (conventional) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Finely grate the potatoes and onion and squeeze well in a cloth.
Mix with the egg, flour, salt and nutmeg.
Place portions on the oiled tray, press flat and bake for 20–25 minutes, turning halfway.
Serve with apple sauce.

title: Swabian Potato Salad with Stock and Chives
instructions: Cook the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes, peel while still warm and slice thinly.
Finely dice the onion.
Stir the hot stock with mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper and pour over the warm potatoes.
Mix in the onion, diced gherkin and rapeseed oil and leave to infuse for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with chives.

title: Sauerkraut and Potato Pan with Smoked Tofu
instructions: Slice the potatoes, dice the smoked tofu and cut the apple into pieces. Dice the onion.
Fry the potatoes in the rapeseed oil for 8 minutes until golden brown and remove from the pan.
Fry the onion and tofu, add the sauerkraut, apple, caraway, bay leaf and juniper and braise for 12 minutes.
Return the potatoes to the pan, mix everything together and season with pepper.

title: Kohlrabi and Carrots in Dill Sauce with Boiled Potatoes
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cook in salted water for 20 minutes.
Cut the kohlrabi and carrots into batons and steam in a little salted water for 10 minutes until tender but firm; reserve 100 ml of the cooking water.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, add the milk and cooking water and simmer for 3 minutes into a sauce.
Add the vegetables to the sauce and season with salt, pepper, nutmeg and plenty of fresh dill.
Serve with the potatoes.

title: Chilled Cucumber and Buttermilk Soup with Dill
instructions: Roughly dice half of the cucumber and blend finely with the buttermilk, dill, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Finely dice the remaining cucumber, the radishes and the cooked potatoes.
Pour the soup into deep plates with the vegetables and chill for at least 20 minutes.
Drizzle with rapeseed oil and serve with rye bread.

title: Courgette and Potato Gratin with Tomatoes and Alpine Cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (conventional). Have a small baking dish ready.
Thinly slice the potatoes and courgette with a mandoline and slice the tomatoes. Brush the dish with the olive oil.
Layer everything in the dish, seasoning each layer with salt, pepper, nutmeg and thyme.
Pour over the milk and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until golden brown.

title: Semolina Pudding with Austrian Plum Compote
instructions: Bring the milk to the boil with the vanilla, sprinkle in the semolina while stirring and leave to swell over low heat for 3–4 minutes.
Stone and quarter the plums and simmer with a splash of water, cinnamon and half of the honey for 8 minutes until soft.
Sweeten the semolina pudding with the remaining honey.
Spoon the pudding into bowls and top with the warm plum compote.

title: Palatschinken (Austrian Crêpes) with Apricots
instructions: Whisk the flour, egg, milk and a pinch of salt into a thin batter and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Stone the apricots, cut into wedges and stew with the honey for 5 minutes until soft.
Brush a pan with a little oil and cook two thin, pale golden pancakes from the batter one after another.
Fill the palatschinken with the apricots, roll up and serve warm.

title: Spelt Muesli with Buttermilk and Pear
instructions: Stir the spelt flakes into the buttermilk in a bowl and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Dice the pear with its skin.
Stir the pear into the muesli.
Top with hazelnuts, honey and cinnamon.

title: Golden Milk with Turmeric, Ginger and Honey
instructions: Slowly heat the milk in a pot with turmeric, grated ginger, cinnamon and a pinch of black pepper; do not boil.
Stir in the almond butter and leave to infuse over low heat for 5 minutes.
Strain into a cup.
Sweeten with honey and drink hot.

title: Kefir and Blueberry Drink with Oats
instructions: Blend the kefir with the blueberries and half of the oats until creamy.
Add the honey and blend briefly.
Pour into a tall glass.
Sprinkle with the remaining oats and a few whole blueberries.

title: Carrot, Orange and Ginger Juice with Linseed Oil
instructions: Peel the carrots, cut into pieces and blend finely with the ginger and a little water in a juicer or high-speed blender.
Peel the orange and blend with the carrot purée.
Pass through a sieve if needed.
Stir in the linseed oil (it helps absorb the beta-carotene), season with lemon juice and drink fresh.

title: Strawberry and Buttermilk Smoothie with Basil
instructions: Wash and hull the strawberries. Set a few aside for garnish.
Blend the strawberries, buttermilk, banana, oats, basil and honey for 1 minute until creamy.
Pour into a glass.
Garnish with strawberry halves and a basil leaf.

title: Light Plum Dumplings with Cinnamon Crumbs
instructions: Cook the potatoes in their skins until soft, peel while still hot and press through a potato ricer. Leave to cool.
Quickly knead with the spelt flour, semolina and a pinch of salt into a smooth dough.
Stone the plums, fill each half with a little sugar and wrap in dough. Shape into two to three dumplings.
Poach the dumplings in gently simmering salted water for 10–12 minutes until cooked.
Melt the butter, toast the grated bread roll with the remaining sugar and cinnamon until golden brown and roll the dumplings in the crumbs.

title: Apple Strudel with Raisins and Walnuts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (conventional). Peel the apples and slice thinly.
Mix the apples with the raisins, walnuts, sugar and cinnamon.
Brush the pastry sheets with melted butter, stack them, spread the filling along one side and roll up.
Place the strudel on a tray lined with baking paper and brush with butter.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden brown, leave to rest for 5 minutes and cut into pieces.

title: Rhubarb Crumble Cake with Spelt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (conventional). The amounts are per piece; for a whole tray simply multiply by 8.
Wash the rhubarb and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Stir the flour, egg, milk, yoghurt, baking powder and half of the sugar into a batter and spread in a tin.
Arrange the rhubarb on top. Rub the butter with the oats, remaining sugar and cinnamon into crumbs and scatter over.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden brown.

title: Oven-Baked Apple Crisps with Walnut and Cinnamon Mix
instructions: Preheat the oven to 100°C (fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Thinly slice the apples with their skin, drizzle with lemon juice and dust with cinnamon.
Lay the slices side by side on the tray and dry for 70–90 minutes, turning halfway.
Leave to cool so they turn crisp. Serve with walnut halves.

title: Asparagus and Strawberry Salad with Rocket and Alpine Cheese
instructions: Peel the lower third of the asparagus, blanch in salted water for 4 minutes, then refresh in cold water.
Cut the asparagus into pieces and quarter the strawberries.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan.
Whisk the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Toss the rocket, asparagus and strawberries in it, top with the cheese and walnuts and serve with rye bread.

title: Tomatoes Stuffed with Buckwheat and Mushrooms
instructions: Cook the buckwheat in twice its volume of salted water for 12 minutes and leave to swell. Preheat the oven to 190°C (conventional).
Cut a lid off each tomato, hollow out and finely chop the flesh.
Fry the onion and mushrooms in the rapeseed oil, add the tomato flesh, buckwheat, sunflower seeds and herbs and season.
Fill the tomatoes, replace the lids and bake for 20 minutes.

title: Austrian Pancake Strip Soup (Frittatensuppe) with Chives
instructions: Whisk the flour, egg, milk, salt and nutmeg into a thin batter and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Cook thin pancakes (frittaten) in a non-stick pan with a little oil until golden.
Thinly slice the carrot and cook in the stock for 8 minutes.
Roll up the pancakes and cut into thin strips.
Place the pancake strips in deep plates, pour over the hot stock and sprinkle with chives.

title: Swabian Bread Pudding (Ofenschlupfer) with Apples and Almonds
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (conventional). Grease a small baking dish with butter.
Thinly slice the bread rolls and cut the apples into wedges.
Layer the rolls, apples and raisins in the dish.
Whisk the milk, egg, sugar, cinnamon and vanilla and pour over. Leave to soak for 10 minutes and sprinkle with the almonds.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden brown.

title: Buckwheat and Mushroom Pan with Leek and Sunflower Seeds
instructions: Cook the buckwheat in twice its volume of salted water for 12 minutes and leave to swell, covered.
Slice the mushrooms, cut the leek into rings and dice the onion.
Fry the onion in the rapeseed oil, add the mushrooms and fry vigorously for 8 minutes.
Add the leek and cook for another 4 minutes.
Mix in the buckwheat and marjoram, season and sprinkle with sunflower seeds and parsley.

title: Buckwheat Kasha with Pear, Walnuts and Linseed
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat in a sieve under hot water and bring to the boil with 150 ml water and a pinch of salt.
Simmer, covered, over low heat for 10 minutes, then add the milk and cinnamon and stir for another 5 minutes until creamy.
Core and dice the pear and fold half into the kasha.
Spoon into a bowl, sprinkle with the remaining pear, chopped walnuts and linseed and drizzle with honey.

title: Huevos Rancheros with Black Beans and Corn Tortilla
instructions: Dice the onion, pepper and tomatoes. Sweat half of the onion with the pepper in half of the oil for 3 minutes, add the tomatoes, cumin and chilli and reduce for 8 minutes into a salsa.
Heat the black beans with the remaining onion and 2 tbsp water and roughly mash.
Briefly toast the tortillas on both sides in a dry pan.
Fry the eggs sunny side up in the remaining oil.
Top the tortillas with the beans, fried egg and salsa and serve with avocado slices, coriander and lime. Drink plenty of fluids with it.

title: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Hash with Kale and Fried Egg
instructions: Wash the sweet potato thoroughly and cut into 1.5 cm cubes with the skin on; slice the onion into strips.
Fry the sweet potato cubes in the oil in a large pan, covered, for 10 minutes, turning occasionally.
Add the onion, chickpeas and paprika and fry uncovered for 5 minutes until crisp.
Strip the kale from the stalks, tear into small pieces and fry for 2 minutes until wilted.
Make a well, crack in the egg and cook, covered, for 3–4 minutes until set. Serve with salt and pepper.

title: Wholegrain Spelt Waffles with Warm Blackberry Compote
instructions: Mix the flour, crushed linseed and baking powder. Whisk the egg, milk and oil, stir in and leave the batter to swell for 10 minutes.
Simmer the blackberries with the maple syrup, a little vanilla and 2 tbsp water in a small pan for 5 minutes until they start to break down.
Preheat the waffle iron and grease lightly.
Bake two golden brown waffles from the batter.
Serve the waffles with the warm blackberry compote.

title: Baked Oats with Raspberries and Hazelnuts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (conventional).
Mash the banana and stir with the oats, yoghurt, milk, baking powder and cinnamon into a thick batter.
Pour the batter into a small ovenproof dish and press the raspberries into it.
Sprinkle with chopped hazelnuts and bake for 22–25 minutes until the top is golden brown and firm.
Leave to cool briefly and eat warm straight from the dish.

title: Dalia – Savoury Indian Cracked Wheat Porridge with Peas and Carrot
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrot and tomato and finely grate the ginger.
Toast the cumin in the oil in a pot for 30 seconds, add the onion and ginger and sweat for 3 minutes.
Stir in the carrot, tomato, turmeric and bulgur and pour in 300 ml water and salt.
Simmer, covered, for 12 minutes until soft, adding the peas after 7 minutes. The porridge should be soft and slightly creamy.
Sprinkle with fresh coriander and serve with a dollop of yoghurt.

title: Swedish Rye Flake Porridge with Apple and Lingonberries
instructions: Bring the rye flakes to the boil with the milk, 80 ml water and a pinch of salt.
Simmer over low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the porridge is creamy, then season with cinnamon and cardamom.
Coarsely grate the apple with its skin and stir in half.
Serve in a bowl with the remaining apple, lingonberries and sunflower seeds.

title: Pumpkin Pancakes with Pecans and Blueberries
instructions: Dice the Hokkaido squash with its skin, steam for 12 minutes until soft and purée finely (or use ready-made purée).
Whisk the pumpkin purée with the egg and milk and stir in the flour, baking powder and spices.
Brush a non-stick pan with the oil and cook small pancakes over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side.
Stack the pancakes, top with blueberries and chopped pecans and drizzle with maple syrup.

title: Oven-Baked Granola with Kiwi and Greek Yoghurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (fan).
Mix the oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds and chia seeds with the maple syrup and oil and spread flat on a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Toast for 15–18 minutes until golden brown, turning once halfway, then leave to cool completely so it turns crisp.
Peel and slice the kiwis.
Put the yoghurt in a glass or bowl and layer the kiwi and granola on top.

title: Cranachan – Scottish Raspberry and Oat Dessert
instructions: Toast the oats in a dry pan for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until golden brown, then leave to cool.
Stir the yoghurt with the honey and a little vanilla until smooth (traditionally a splash of whisky is added; this version is without).
Mash a third of the raspberries with a fork.
Layer the yoghurt, mashed and whole raspberries and toasted oats alternately in a tall glass, finishing with raspberries and oats.

title: Poached Pear with Dark Cocoa Sauce and Almonds
instructions: Peel the pears, leaving the stalk on, and cut the base flat.
Place in a small pan with just enough water to cover, the cinnamon stick, vanilla and lemon zest and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes until soft.
Toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan until golden brown.
Heat the milk, stir in the cocoa and maple syrup until smooth and simmer for 1 minute until thickened.
Stand the pears on a plate, pour over the cocoa sauce and sprinkle with almonds.

title: Artichoke and Bean Dip with Vegetable Sticks
instructions: Rinse and drain the beans.
Blend the beans, artichoke hearts, garlic, half of the olive oil, lemon juice and 2 tbsp water until creamy and season with salt and pepper.
Peel the carrots and kohlrabi and cut into sticks.
Spoon the dip into a bowl, garnish with the remaining olive oil, parsley and chilli flakes and serve with the vegetable sticks. Drink plenty of fluids with it.

title: Guacamole with Oven-Baked Tortilla Chips and Pepper Sticks
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (conventional). Cut the tortillas into triangles, salt lightly and bake on the tray for 7–9 minutes until crisp.
Roughly mash the avocado with a fork and mix with lime juice and salt.
Finely dice the tomato and onion and fold into the avocado with coriander and a little chilli.
Cut the pepper into sticks and serve with the chips alongside the guacamole.

title: Chocolate Avocado Mousse with Raspberries
instructions: Blend the avocado, banana, cocoa, maple syrup, oat drink, vanilla and a pinch of salt in a blender or with a stick blender until very smooth.
Taste and add a little more maple syrup if needed.
Spoon the mousse into a glass and chill for at least 20 minutes.
Serve with fresh raspberries.

title: Gajar Halwa – Indian Carrot Dessert with Pistachios
instructions: Sweat the carrots in the butter in a pot for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the milk and reduce over medium heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until almost no liquid remains.
Stir in the chopped dates, cardamom and almonds and keep stirring for 3 minutes.
Serve warm or lukewarm in a bowl, sprinkled with pistachios.

title: Cinnamon Popcorn with Almonds and Apple Wedges
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot, add the popcorn kernels and put the lid on.
Let them pop over medium heat, shaking occasionally, until only the odd kernel still pops.
Stir the maple syrup with the cinnamon, drizzle over the warm popcorn and toss with the almonds.
Cut the apple into wedges and serve alongside the popcorn.

title: Fruit Salad with Kiwi, Pear, Blackberries and Hemp Seeds
instructions: Peel the kiwis and cut into half-moons; core the pear and dice it with its skin.
Briefly rinse and drain the blackberries.
Mix the fruit in a bowl and drizzle with the freshly squeezed orange juice.
Sprinkle with hemp seeds and chopped mint and serve immediately.

title: Pear and Ginger Smoothie with Oats and Almonds
instructions: Core the pears and roughly dice them with the skin; peel the ginger.
Soak the oats in the oat drink for 5 minutes.
Blend all the ingredients with 50 ml cold water for 1 minute until very smooth.
Pour into a large glass and dust with a pinch of cinnamon.

title: Green Kiwi and Avocado Smoothie with Cucumber and Apple
instructions: Peel the kiwis, core the apple and dice it with its skin, and roughly chop the cucumber.
Put all the ingredients in the blender with 100 ml cold water.
Blend on the highest setting for 1 minute until the smoothie is completely smooth.
Pour into a glass immediately and drink.

title: Raspberry and Blackberry Smoothie with Oat Drink and Banana
instructions: Peel the banana and break into pieces.
Put the frozen berries in the blender with the banana and oat drink.
Blend for 1 minute until creamy, adding a splash of water if needed.
Pour into a glass and garnish with a few berries.

title: Pumpernickel with Goat's Cheese, Fig and Walnuts
instructions: Spread the pumpernickel slices with the goat's cheese.
Slice the figs and arrange on top.
Roughly chop the walnuts and scatter over.
Top with rocket, drizzle with honey and season with thyme and pepper.

title: Beetroot and Bean Spread on Crispbread with Cress
instructions: Rinse and drain the kidney beans; roughly dice the beetroot.
Blend the beans, beetroot, olive oil, garlic, cumin and lemon juice until creamy and season with salt and pepper.
Spread the crispbread thickly with the spread.
Top with cucumber slices and sprinkle with cress. Drink plenty of fluids with it.

title: Pea and Mint Smash with Smoked Trout on Wholegrain Rye Bread
ingredients: Fresh mint, lemon juice, chilli flakes
instructions: Cook the peas in boiling salted water for 3 minutes, drain and briefly refresh in cold water.
Roughly crush the peas with a fork together with olive oil, chopped mint, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toast the bread and spread thickly with the pea smash.
Flake the smoked trout, thinly slice the radishes, arrange both on top and sprinkle with chilli flakes and mint.

title: Edamame and Wasabi Spread on Wholegrain Bread with Cucumber and Sesame
instructions: Cook the edamame in salted water for 4 minutes and drain, reserving 3 tbsp of the cooking water.
Blend the edamame with soy sauce, a little wasabi, lime juice and the cooking water into a creamy, slightly chunky paste.
Spread the wholegrain bread thickly with the spread.
Thinly slice the cucumber, arrange on top and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.

title: Mushroom and Lentil Pâté on Rye Bread with Cornichons
instructions: Cook the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until soft and drain.
Finely chop the onion and mushrooms and fry with the garlic and thyme in the oil for 8–10 minutes until the liquid has evaporated.
Process the mushrooms, lentils and walnuts in a mini chopper into a spreadable, slightly coarse pâté and season well with salt and pepper.
Spread on the rye bread and serve with cornichons.

title: Spelt Risotto (Dinkotto) with Artichokes, Lemon and Hard Cheese
ingredients: Lemon zest and juice, salt, pepper
instructions: Finely dice the onion and garlic and sweat in the olive oil until translucent. Add the pearled spelt and toast for 1 minute.
Gradually add hot stock and cook the spelt for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until creamy.
Quarter the artichoke hearts, fold in for the last 5 minutes and heat through.
Stir in the hard cheese, lemon zest and a little lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.
Spoon onto plates and serve topped with rocket.

title: Salmon on Puy Lentils with Leek and Carrots
ingredients: Thyme, white wine vinegar, salt, pepper
instructions: Rinse the lentils and cook with thyme in the stock and a little water for 20–25 minutes until tender but firm.
Cut the leek into rings and the carrot and shallot into fine dice and sweat in half of the oil for 6 minutes.
Mix the vegetables with the lentils, stir in the mustard and a splash of vinegar and season.
Salt the salmon and fry skin side down in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until crisp, turn and finish cooking for 1–2 minutes.
Spoon the lentils onto plates and place the salmon on top, skin side up.

title: Chicken Tinga with Black Beans and Corn Tortillas
instructions: Poach the chicken breast in salted water for 15 minutes and shred with two forks.
Slice the onion into strips and fry in the rapeseed oil until soft. Purée the tomatoes and chipotle, add and reduce with the oregano for 5 minutes.
Toss the chicken in the sauce. Warm the beans separately and roughly mash.
Heat the tortillas in a dry pan and top with the beans and tinga.
Serve with red cabbage, avocado slices, coriander and lime.

title: Ghormeh Sabzi – Persian Herb Stew with Beef, Kidney Beans and Rice
ingredients: Dried lime, turmeric, fenugreek leaves, salt
instructions: Dice the onion and fry in half of the oil until golden brown. Add the beef and turmeric and brown all over.
Pour in 400 ml water, add the pierced dried lime and braise, covered, for 50 minutes.
Finely chop the herbs, leek greens and spinach and sweat in the remaining oil with the fenugreek for 8 minutes until dark green.
Add the herbs and kidney beans to the meat and simmer for another 20 minutes.
Cook the basmati rice and serve with the stew.

title: Jerusalem Artichoke and Parsnip Soup with Hazelnuts and Wholegrain Bread
instructions: Scrub the Jerusalem artichokes thoroughly, peel the parsnip and roughly dice both with the onion.
Sweat the vegetables in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes, pour in the stock and simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Add the oat drink and blend everything until smooth. Season with nutmeg, marjoram, salt and pepper.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan and roughly chop.
Sprinkle the soup with the hazelnuts and serve with the wholegrain bread. Drink plenty of fluids with it.

title: Nasu Dengaku – Miso Aubergine with Edamame and Brown Rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice its volume of water for 30–35 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Halve the aubergine lengthways, score the flesh in a diamond pattern, brush with rapeseed oil and bake cut side up for 20 minutes.
Stir the miso with the maple syrup, sesame oil and 1 tbsp water until smooth, spread over the aubergines and caramelise under the grill for 4 minutes.
Cook the edamame in salted water for 4 minutes.
Sprinkle the aubergines with sesame seeds and spring onions and serve with the rice and edamame.

title: Beef Bulgogi with Barley Rice, Spinach Namul and Kimchi
instructions: Mix the beef with soy sauce, grated pear and garlic and marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Rinse the rice and pearl barley together and cook with 200 ml water for 25 minutes (bori-bap).
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately for 1 minute each, squeeze out and dress with sesame oil, sesame seeds and salt. Cut the carrot into strips.
Sear the meat in a very hot pan for 2–3 minutes.
Serve the barley rice with the bulgogi, namul, carrot and kimchi.

title: Aloo Gobi with Peas and Wholemeal Chapati
ingredients: Cumin, turmeric, garam masala, coriander, salt
instructions: Knead the wholemeal flour with a pinch of salt and about 30 ml water into a smooth dough and leave to rest for 15 minutes.
Toast the cumin in the rapeseed oil, add the onion and ginger and fry for 4 minutes. Stir in the tomato and turmeric.
Add the cauliflower florets and diced potato and cook, covered, with 80 ml water for 15 minutes. Add the peas and garam masala and cook uncovered for another 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into two pieces, roll out thinly and cook in a hot dry pan for 1 minute per side until it blisters.
Sprinkle the aloo gobi with coriander and serve with the chapatis.

title: Hake on Bean and Fennel Ragout
instructions: Cut the fennel into thin strips, dice the tomatoes and chop the garlic.
Sweat the fennel and garlic in half of the olive oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes, paprika, saffron and stock and simmer for 8 minutes.
Fold in the beans, warm for 3 minutes and season with salt.
Salt the hake and fry in the remaining oil for 3 minutes per side.
Divide the ragout between deep plates, place the fish on top and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Pan-Fried Mackerel with Barley, Kale and Pear Salad
instructions: Cook the pearl barley in three times its volume of salted water for 25 minutes and drain.
Cut the kale into thin strips and massage with a pinch of salt by hand for 1 minute until soft.
Stir together the mustard, vinegar and rapeseed oil. Cut the pear into wedges and the onion into thin rings and mix with the barley, kale and dressing.
Fry the mackerel skin side down in a hot dry pan for 4 minutes until crisp, turn and finish cooking for 1 minute.
Sprinkle the salad with toasted walnuts and place the mackerel on top.

title: Prawn and Okra Gumbo with Brown Rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice its volume of water for 30–35 minutes.
Toast the rapeseed oil and flour in a pot for 8–10 minutes, stirring constantly, into a hazelnut-brown roux.
Dice the onion, pepper and celery, add and sweat for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, stock, Cajun seasoning, thyme and bay leaf.
Slice the okra, add and simmer for 20 minutes until the gumbo has thickened.
Poach the prawns in it for the last 4 minutes. Serve with the rice.

title: Turkey Breast with Wild Rice, Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Lingonberries
instructions: Cook the wild rice in plenty of salted water for 40 minutes and drain.
Preheat the oven to 210°C. Halve the Brussels sprouts, cut the onion into wedges, toss with half of the oil, salt and pepper and roast for 25 minutes.
Season the turkey breast with sage, thyme, salt and pepper and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side, then leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop and briefly toast the pecans and fold into the wild rice with the Brussels sprouts.
Slice the turkey, arrange on the wild rice and serve with lingonberries.

title: Freekeh with Chicken, Chickpeas and Almonds
instructions: Dice the onion and fry in half of the olive oil until golden brown. Add the freekeh and baharat and toast for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and 100 ml water and cook, covered, for 20 minutes. Fold in the chickpeas for the last 5 minutes.
Season the chicken breast with baharat, cinnamon and salt and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side, rest briefly and cut into strips.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden brown.
Serve the freekeh with the chicken, sprinkle with almonds and parsley and serve with yoghurt.

title: Lupin Patties with Red Cabbage and Apple Salad and Potatoes
ingredients: Parsley, marjoram, cider vinegar, salt, pepper
instructions: Pour 80 ml hot water over the lupin grits and leave to swell for 10 minutes. Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes.
Finely shred the red cabbage and briefly knead with salt; cut the apple into matchsticks and mix with the cider vinegar and 1 tsp oil.
Finely dice the onion and knead with the lupin grits, oats, mustard, marjoram, parsley, salt and pepper. Shape four flat patties.
Fry the patties in the remaining rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve with the red cabbage and apple salad and the potatoes.

title: Wholewheat Orecchiette with Broccoli, Anchovies and Chilli
instructions: Divide the broccoli into small florets; peel and dice the stalk.
Cook the orecchiette in plenty of salted water, adding the broccoli halfway through the cooking time, and cook everything together until al dente.
Heat the olive oil with the garlic, anchovies and chilli until the anchovies break down.
Add the pasta and broccoli to the pan with a little cooking water and toss until the broccoli partly breaks down and forms a sauce.
Serve with lemon zest and Parmesan.

title: Red-Red – Ghanaian Black-Eyed Bean Stew with Baked Plantain
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Peel the plantain, slice diagonally, brush with 1 tsp oil and bake for 20 minutes until golden brown, turning once.
Dice the onion and fry in the remaining oil with ginger, chilli and paprika for 5 minutes.
Briefly toast the tomato purée, dice the tomatoes, add and reduce for 10 minutes into a thick red sauce.
Fold in the beans, simmer for 8 minutes and season with salt.
Serve the beans with the baked plantain.

title: Babgulyás – Hungarian Bean Goulash Soup with Beef
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the rapeseed oil until golden. Cut the beef into small cubes, add and brown all over.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, caraway and tomato purée, then pour in the stock and simmer, covered, for 40 minutes.
Dice the carrot, parsnip, potato and pepper, add and cook for another 20 minutes.
Add the beans and cook for 5 minutes. Season with marjoram and salt.
Serve in deep plates or soup bowls.

title: Çılbır – Poached Eggs on Garlic Yoghurt with Spinach Bulgur
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the olive oil, stir in the tomato purée and bulgur, pour in 150 ml water and leave to swell, covered, for 12 minutes.
Roughly chop the spinach and fold into the bulgur until wilted. Season with salt.
Stir the yoghurt with grated garlic and a pinch of salt and spread on a plate.
Poach the eggs in simmering vinegar water for 3–4 minutes and place on the yoghurt.
Foam the butter with pul biber (Aleppo pepper flakes), drizzle over the eggs, sprinkle with dill and serve with the spinach bulgur.

title: Gigantes Plaki – Greek Baked Giant Beans with Feta
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Finely dice the onion, carrot, celery and garlic and sweat in the olive oil for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 5 minutes. Fold in the beans and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer everything to a small baking dish and bake for 30 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the beans on top are lightly toasted.
Crumble the feta over, sprinkle with dill and serve with the bread.

title: Fattoush with Chickpeas and Toasted Wholemeal Pitta
instructions: Tear the pitta into bite-sized pieces and toast in the oven at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Rinse the chickpeas, pat dry and toast with sumac in a dry pan for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes and pepper and pick the herb leaves.
Stir the olive oil with lemon juice, sumac and salt and toss with the vegetables, chickpeas and herbs.
Just before serving, fold in the pitta chips and sprinkle with pomegranate seeds.

title: Santorini Fava with Grilled Squid and Capers
instructions: Wash the split peas thoroughly and bring to the boil with the onion, garlic and stock. Skim and simmer, covered, for 40 minutes until very soft.
Blend until smooth with half of the olive oil, the lemon juice and salt.
Clean the inside of the squid, score in a diamond pattern, season with oregano and salt and grill in a very hot griddle pan with a little oil for 1–2 minutes per side.
Spread the fava on plates, place the squid on top and finish with capers, red onion rings and the remaining oil.
Serve with tomato wedges and lemon.

title: Massaman Curry with Tofu, Squash and Peanuts
ingredients: Massaman curry paste (vegan, no shrimp paste)
instructions: Cook the jasmine rice according to the packet instructions. Dice the tofu and fry in a dry non-stick pan until golden brown all over.
Toast the curry paste in a pot with 2 tbsp coconut milk until fragrant.
