Dice the squash, potatoes and onion, add, pour in the remaining coconut milk and 150 ml water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the pepper, tofu and spinach and cook for 5 minutes. Season with tamarind, lime and soy sauce.
Sprinkle with toasted peanuts and serve with the rice.

title: Lamb Fillet with Pea and Mint Purée, Rosemary Potatoes and Carrots
ingredients: Fresh mint, rosemary, lemon, salt, pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C. Quarter the potatoes, toss with half of the oil, rosemary and salt and roast for 25 minutes. Add the carrot batons after 10 minutes.
Cook the peas in a little salted water for 4 minutes, drain and roughly purée with the yoghurt, mint and a squeeze of lemon.
Season the lamb fillet with salt and pepper and fry in the remaining oil for 6–8 minutes all over until pink, then leave to rest for 3 minutes.
Slice the lamb and serve with the pea purée, rosemary potatoes and carrots.

title: Lentil and Mushroom Shepherd's Pie with Sweet Potato Topping
instructions: Wash the sweet potato thoroughly, dice with its skin, cook in salted water for 15 minutes until soft and roughly mash.
Finely dice the onion, carrot and mushrooms and fry vigorously in the rapeseed oil for 6 minutes. Briefly toast the tomato purée.
Add the lentils, stock, soy sauce and herbs and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft and the filling is thick.
Transfer the filling to a baking dish, spread the sweet potato mash on top and draw grooves with a fork.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until the topping is golden brown. Keeps for 3 days in portions in the fridge.

title: Tofu Bánh Mì with Pickled Vegetables and Coriander
instructions: Cut the carrot and radish into fine matchsticks and pickle them with the rice vinegar, maple syrup and a pinch of salt for at least 15 minutes.
Cut the tofu into 1 cm thick slices, pat dry thoroughly and marinate in the soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Fry the tofu in the rapeseed oil for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden brown.
Slice the baguette open lengthways and crisp it up briefly in the oven.
Fill with the tofu, drained vegetables, cucumber strips, chilli rings and coriander, and drizzle with sriracha.

title: Tempeh Balado – Tempeh in Chilli-Tomato Sambal with Rice and Green Beans
instructions: Cook the jasmine rice according to the packet instructions. Trim the green beans and cook in salted water for 6 minutes until al dente.
Cut the tempeh into thin slices and fry in half of the oil for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Roughly blitz the chillies, shallots, garlic and tomatoes into a paste in a blender.
Cook the paste down in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until it is a glossy deep red. Season with the sugar, salt and lime juice.
Add the tempeh to the sambal, toss briefly and serve with the rice and beans.

title: Seitan Stroganoff with Mushrooms and Wholewheat Tagliatelle
instructions: Cook the tagliatelle in salted water according to the packet instructions.
Cut the seitan into thin strips, sear in half of the oil over high heat for 4 minutes and set aside.
Cut the onion into strips and slice the mushrooms, then fry in the remaining oil for 6 minutes. Briefly toast the paprika with them.
Deglaze with the stock, stir in the mustard and reduce for 3 minutes. Lower the heat, stir in the soy yoghurt and seitan and only warm through – do not boil.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the pasta and parsley.

title: Hong Shao Tofu – Red-Braised Tofu with Shiitake, Pak Choi and Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes, pat dry and fry in the oil until golden brown all over, then set aside.
Sweat the ginger, garlic and the white part of the spring onion in the remaining oil and lightly caramelise the sugar in it.
Add the sliced shiitake, deglaze with the soy sauce, star anise and 120 ml water, and return the tofu to the pan.
Braise covered for 10 minutes, then reduce uncovered until the sauce glazes the tofu.
Halve the pak choi, steam for 2 minutes and arrange with the tofu, rice and spring onion greens.

title: Tofu Tikka Masala with Basmati Rice
ingredients: Garam masala, turmeric, paprika, dried fenugreek leaves, coriander
instructions: Dice the tofu, mix with the soy yoghurt, garam masala, paprika and salt and marinate for 15 minutes.
Roast the tofu on a lined baking tray at 220°C for 15 minutes until the edges darken. Cook the basmati rice.
Finely chop the onion, ginger and garlic and fry in the oil for 6 minutes until golden brown. Briefly toast the turmeric and garam masala with them.
Add the passata and reduce for 10 minutes, then stir in the coconut milk and crumbled fenugreek leaves.
Add the tofu to the sauce, let it infuse for 2 minutes and serve with the rice and coriander.

title: Cuban Picadillo with Soy Mince, Olives, Raisins and Rice
instructions: Pour the hot stock over the soy mince and leave to soak for 10 minutes. Cook the rice.
Finely dice the onion, pepper and garlic and sweat in the olive oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the soaked mince with its liquid and fry for 4 minutes until crumbly. Stir in the cumin and oregano.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaf, halved olives and raisins and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Season with salt and serve with the rice.

title: Lentil Sloppy Joes on Wholegrain Rolls with Coleslaw
instructions: Boil the lentils in plenty of water for 20–25 minutes until tender, then drain.
Finely shred the white cabbage, grate the carrot and knead well with the cider vinegar, salt and a pinch of sugar.
Finely dice the onion and pepper and fry in the oil for 5 minutes. Briefly toast the tomato purée and smoked paprika with them.
Add the lentils, passata, mustard and maple syrup and cook down for 8 minutes into a thick, juicy mixture.
Slice the rolls open, toast them, fill with the lentil mixture and serve with the coleslaw.

title: Pasta e Ceci – Roman Pasta with Chickpeas and Rosemary
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery and sweat with the garlic and rosemary in half of the olive oil for 6 minutes.
Briefly toast the tomato purée, add the chickpeas and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Purée a third of the chickpeas with a little liquid and return to the pan.
Cook the pasta directly in the soup for 10 minutes, stirring, until al dente and creamy.
Season with salt, pepper and chilli and serve drizzled with the remaining olive oil.

title: Vegan Cassoulet with White Beans, Smoked Tofu and Herb Crumbs
ingredients: Thyme, bay leaf, parsley, salt, pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Dice the smoked tofu and fry in half of the oil for 4 minutes until crisp.
Dice the onion, carrot, celery and garlic and sweat briefly with the tofu.
Add the beans, tomatoes, stock, thyme and bay leaf, season with salt and pepper and transfer everything to a small baking dish.
Mix the panko with chopped parsley and the remaining oil and sprinkle over the top.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and the crumbs are golden brown.

title: Seitan with Mojo Verde and Papas Arrugadas
instructions: Cook the potatoes in their skins in heavily salted water for 20 minutes, drain and let them dry in the pan until a salt crust forms.
For the mojo verde, finely purée the herbs, pepper, garlic, cumin, vinegar and 10 g olive oil with 2 tbsp water.
Slice the seitan and sear in the remaining oil in a griddle pan for 3 minutes per side.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and season with salt.
Arrange the seitan with the potatoes, salad and plenty of mojo verde.

title: Kongguksu – Korean Cold Soy Milk Noodles with Cucumber and Tomato
instructions: Blend the tofu, soy drink and 8 g sesame seeds until very smooth, season with salt and chill for at least 20 minutes.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Cut the cucumber into fine strips and the tomato into wedges.
Place the noodles in a deep bowl, pour over the ice-cold soy soup and add a few ice cubes.
Top with the cucumber, tomato and remaining sesame seeds.

title: Tofu Katsu Curry with Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Cut the onion into strips and the carrot and potato into cubes, and sweat in 3 g oil for 5 minutes.
Dust with 8 g flour and the curry powder, toast briefly, deglaze with the stock, add the apple and soy sauce and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Cut the tofu into two flat slices, pat dry and coat first in the remaining flour, then in the soy drink and finally in the panko.
Drizzle the tofu katsu with the remaining oil and bake on baking paper for 18 minutes until golden brown and crisp, turning once.
Slice the katsu into strips and serve with the rice and curry sauce.

title: Tofu Larb with Sticky Rice and Crunchy Raw Vegetables
ingredients: Glutinous rice (uncooked, incl. 10 g for toasted rice powder)
instructions: Soak 50 g glutinous rice for at least 4 hours and steam for 25 minutes.
Toast 10 g glutinous rice in a dry pan until golden brown and grind to a coarse powder in a mortar.
Finely crumble the tofu and fry in the oil for 8 minutes until dry and slightly crisp.
Take the pan off the heat and mix the tofu with the lime juice, soy sauce, chilli, shallot rings, spring onion, herbs and toasted rice powder.
Serve with the sticky rice, cucumber, beans and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

title: Mercimek Köftesi – Red Lentil and Bulgur Patties with Salad and Pomegranate
ingredients: Pul biber (Aleppo pepper), cumin, lemon, salt
instructions: Cook the lentils in 180 ml water for 15 minutes until soft and the water is almost absorbed. Remove from the heat, stir in the bulgur and leave to swell, covered, for 20 minutes.
Finely dice the onion and sweat in the olive oil for 5 minutes until soft. Briefly toast the tomato and pepper paste, pul biber and cumin with it.
Knead the onion mixture, chopped spring onion, parsley, lemon juice and salt into the lentil and bulgur mixture.
With wet hands, shape into oblong patties, pressing them with your fingers.
Arrange on lettuce leaves, sprinkle with pomegranate seeds and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Githeri – Kenyan Corn and Bean Stew with Potatoes and Kale
instructions: Dice the onion and garlic and fry in the oil for 5 minutes until golden. Briefly toast the curry powder with them.
Dice the tomatoes, add them and cook for 5 minutes until they break down into a sauce.
Dice the potatoes and carrot, add with the corn, beans and stock and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Cut the kale into fine strips, fold in and cook for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt and serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Green Spelt Patties with Creamed Savoy Cabbage and Potatoes
instructions: Bring the cracked green spelt to the boil in the stock and leave to swell, covered, for 15 minutes, then let it cool. Cook the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes.
Finely dice the onion and knead into the green spelt with the carrot, chickpea flour, mustard, marjoram, salt and pepper. Leave the mixture to rest for 10 minutes and shape into 3 patties.
Fry the patties in 7 g oil for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Cut the savoy cabbage into fine strips, sweat in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, add the cooking cream, season with nutmeg and reduce for 3 minutes.
Serve the patties with the creamed savoy cabbage and parsley potatoes.

title: Harira – Moroccan Tomato Soup with Lentils, Chickpeas and Dates
ingredients: Ras el hanout, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, lemon
instructions: Finely dice the onion and celery and sweat in the olive oil for 5 minutes. Briefly toast the spices and tomato purée with them.
Add the tomatoes, lentils and stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and vermicelli and cook for another 6 minutes.
Mix the flour with 4 tbsp water until smooth, pour it in while stirring and simmer the soup for 3 minutes until thickened. Stir in the chopped herbs.
Serve with lemon wedges and dates, as is customary during Ramadan.

title: Tempeh Tacos al Pastor with Pineapple and Red Cabbage
instructions: Soak the chillies in hot water for 10 minutes and purée finely with the orange juice, cumin, oregano, achiote and salt.
Cut the tempeh into thin strips, mix with the marinade and leave to infuse for 15 minutes.
Fry the tempeh in the oil for 6 minutes until the marinade caramelises. Cut the pineapple into small cubes and fry with it for the last 2 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Top with the tempeh, pineapple, diced onion, red cabbage and coriander and serve with lime.

title: Rajma Chawal – Punjabi Kidney Bean Curry with Rice and Cucumber Raita
ingredients: Cumin, garam masala, turmeric, chilli, coriander
instructions: Cook the basmati rice. Toast the cumin in the oil, finely dice the onion and fry for 8 minutes until golden brown.
Grate the ginger and garlic, add with the turmeric, chilli and garam masala and toast for 1 minute.
Purée the tomatoes, add them and reduce for 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the beans and 150 ml water, mash a few beans and simmer for 15 minutes until creamy.
Grate the cucumber, mix with the soy yoghurt, cumin and salt, and serve with the rajma, rice and coriander.

title: Thukpa – Tibetan Noodle Soup with Tofu and Vegetables
instructions: Dice the tofu, fry in the oil until browned all over and set aside.
Chop the onion, ginger and garlic and sweat for 3 minutes. Dice the tomato and cook for 2 minutes until it breaks down.
Add the stock and soy sauce, then the sliced carrot and shredded cabbage, and simmer for 8 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately, drain and place in a large bowl. Let the spinach and tofu warm through in the soup for 1 minute.
Ladle the soup over the noodles and sprinkle with spring onion and chilli.

title: Tofu Bhurji with Tomatoes, Peas, Spinach and Wholegrain Pav
ingredients: Green chilli, turmeric, cumin, kala namak (black salt), coriander
instructions: Toast the cumin in the oil, then fry the finely chopped onion, ginger and chilli for 3 minutes. Dice the tomato and cook for 2 minutes.
Roughly crumble the tofu with your fingers, add with the turmeric and peas and fry for 5 minutes.
Fold in the spinach and let it wilt. Season with kala namak and coriander.
Slice the rolls open and toast in a dry pan for 1 minute on each side.
Serve the bhurji with the warm pav, Mumbai-style, for filling or dipping.

title: Chickpea Omelette with Mushrooms, Spinach and Chives
ingredients: Kala namak (black salt), turmeric, baking powder, chives, pepper
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour with the water, nutritional yeast, turmeric, a pinch of baking powder and kala namak until smooth and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Dice the shallot, slice the mushrooms and fry in half of the oil for 5 minutes. Briefly wilt the spinach and set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the batter and let it set over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Place the mushroom and spinach filling on one half, fold the omelette over and fry for another 1 minute.
Sprinkle with chives and serve with toasted sourdough bread.

title: Natto Gohan with Miso Soup and Cucumber Tsukemono
instructions: Wash the rice and cook with 90 ml water for 15 minutes, then leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Thinly slice the cucumber, knead with a little salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out.
Heat 300 ml kombu dashi, dice the silken tofu and warm it in the dashi with the wakame. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the miso – do not let it boil again.
Stir the natto vigorously with the soy sauce until it forms strings and place on the rice.
Serve with spring onion, nori strips, the miso soup and the cucumber.

title: Fatteh – Lebanese Chickpeas with Pitta Chips and Tahini Soy Yoghurt
instructions: Tear the pitta into pieces and toast in the oven at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Heat the chickpeas with 50 ml water, cumin and salt for 5 minutes.
Stir the soy yoghurt with the tahini, grated garlic, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Toast the pine nuts in the olive oil until golden brown.
Place the pitta chips in a bowl, top with the warm chickpeas and a little of their liquid, pour over the tahini yoghurt and finish with the pine nuts, paprika, parsley and pomegranate.

title: Beans on Toast with Mushrooms and Spinach
instructions: Finely dice the onion and sweat in 2 g oil until translucent. Briefly toast the tomato purée with it.
Add the passata, maple syrup, smoked paprika and beans and simmer for 8 minutes until thick. Season to taste.
Quarter the mushrooms and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until browned, add the spinach and let it wilt.
Toast the bread until golden brown.
Spoon the beans onto the toast and serve with the mushrooms and spinach.

title: Buckwheat Blini with Soy Yoghurt and Blueberries
instructions: Mix the linseeds with 2 tbsp water and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Mix the buckwheat flour, baking powder and salt, stir in the soy drink and linseeds and leave the batter to rest for 10 minutes.
Brush a pan with a little oil and add one tablespoon of batter per blini. Cook over medium heat for 1–2 minutes per side.
Make 8 small blini this way.
Serve with the soy yoghurt, blueberries and maple syrup.

title: Tapioca – Brazilian Cassava Crêpe with Banana, Peanut Butter and Cinnamon
instructions: Sift the tapioca flour evenly into a dry non-stick pan.
Cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until the starch sticks together into a flatbread, then turn and cook for another 1 minute.
Slice the banana, place on one half, drizzle with the peanut butter and dust with cinnamon.
Fold the crêpe over and serve with the soy yoghurt.

title: Akara – Nigerian Bean Fritters with Tomato-Pepper Sauce and Wholegrain Bread
instructions: Soak the black-eyed beans overnight, rub off the skins and purée with half of the onion, the chilli, salt and 3 tbsp water into a light batter. Beat vigorously for 3 minutes.
Fry tablespoons of the batter in 10 g hot oil in a pan for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Purée the tomatoes, pepper and remaining onion and cook down in the remaining oil for 10 minutes into a thick sauce.
Serve the akara hot with the sauce and wholegrain bread – Nigerian-style, ideally as a sandwich.

title: Molletes with Black Beans, Avocado and Pico de Gallo
instructions: Heat the black beans with the cumin, salt and 3 tbsp water and mash into a coarse purée.
Halve the rolls, spread with the bean purée, sprinkle with nutritional yeast and bake in the oven at 220°C for 6 minutes.
Finely dice the tomato, onion, jalapeño and coriander and mix with the lime juice and salt to make pico de gallo.
Top the molletes with the pico de gallo and avocado slices.

title: Amaranth Porridge with Mango, Coconut and Hemp Seeds
instructions: Rinse the amaranth in a fine sieve and bring to the boil with 100 ml water and half of the soy drink.
Simmer covered over low heat for 20 minutes until the grains are tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the remaining soy drink, the vanilla and maple syrup and stir for 2 minutes until creamy.
Dice the mango. Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the mango, desiccated coconut, hemp seeds and lime zest.

title: Spelt Banana Bread Muffins with Walnuts and Soy Yoghurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Mix the linseeds with 2 tbsp water and leave to swell.
Mash the banana and mix with the linseeds, maple syrup, soy drink and oil.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt, then stir in two thirds of the chopped walnuts.
Divide the batter between 2 muffin cases, sprinkle with the remaining walnuts and bake for 22 minutes.
Leave to cool slightly and serve with the soy yoghurt.

title: Tempeh TLT Sandwich with Tomato, Lettuce and Avocado
instructions: Cut the tempeh into very thin slices. Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup and smoked paprika.
Fry the tempeh in the oil for 2 minutes per side until crisp, deglaze with the marinade and glaze until it has evaporated.
Toast the bread and spread one slice with mashed avocado.
Top with lettuce, tomato slices and tempeh, cover with the second slice and cut in half diagonally.

title: Xian Doujiang – Taiwanese Savoury Soy Milk Soup with Flatbread
instructions: Finely dice the smoked tofu and slice the spring onion into rings.
Put the rice vinegar, soy sauce, tofu and half of the spring onion into a soup bowl.
Heat the soy drink until almost boiling and pour it briskly into the bowl. Wait briefly until the soy milk sets slightly and forms curds.
Top with the chilli sesame oil, white pepper and remaining spring onion.
Briefly toast the flatbread and serve alongside for dipping.

title: Tofu Benedict with Spinach and Cashew Hollandaise
ingredients: Turmeric, kala namak (black salt), lemon juice, chives
instructions: Soak the cashews for at least 2 hours, drain and blend with the soy drink, nutritional yeast, mustard, turmeric, lemon juice and kala namak into a smooth hollandaise. Warm gently.
Cut the tofu into two round slices 1.5 cm thick, season with turmeric and kala namak and fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side until golden yellow.
Wilt the spinach in the pan. Halve and toast the rolls, and slice the tomato.
Top the roll halves with tomato, spinach and tofu and coat with the hollandaise. Sprinkle with chives.

title: Bubur Kacang Hijau – Indonesian Mung Bean and Coconut Porridge with Banana
instructions: Soak the mung beans for 2 hours and drain.
Bring to the boil with 400 ml water, ginger slices and pandan and simmer for 30 minutes until the beans burst and turn creamy.
Stir in the sugar and a pinch of salt and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Briefly warm the coconut milk with a pinch of salt.
Spoon the porridge into bowls, pour over the coconut milk and top with banana slices and sesame seeds.

title: Muhammara – Syrian Red Pepper and Walnut Dip with Vegetable Sticks and Pitta
instructions: Roast the peppers at 230°C for 25 minutes until the skin blisters black, leave to cool covered and peel.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan. Coarsely purée with the peppers, breadcrumbs, pomegranate molasses, cumin, Aleppo pepper, lemon juice and salt.
Spread the dip into a bowl and drizzle with olive oil.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks, toast the pitta and cut into triangles, and serve both with the dip.

title: Cocoa Tahini Energy Balls with Dates and Sesame
instructions: Soak the dates in warm water for 10 minutes and drain well.
Process the dates with the tahini, oats, cocoa and salt in a mini chopper into a sticky mixture.
With wet hands, shape into 4 balls.
Roll in sesame seeds and chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Funghi Ripieni – Stuffed Mushrooms with White Bean and Walnut Filling
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Twist the stalks out of the mushrooms and chop finely.
Fry the mushroom stalks and garlic in half of the oil for 3 minutes. Roughly mash the beans with a fork, chop the walnuts and parsley and mix everything with the lemon zest, oregano, salt and pepper.
Press the filling into the mushroom caps. Finely crumble the bread, mix with the remaining oil and sprinkle over the top.
Bake on a tray for 15–18 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the crumbs golden brown. Serve warm or lukewarm.

title: Pimientos de Padrón with Toasted Almonds, Lemon and Sea Salt
instructions: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 4 minutes and chop roughly.
Heat the olive oil in the pan until very hot and fry the peppers for 4–5 minutes until the skin blisters and darkens in places.
Immediately sprinkle with coarse sea salt and the almonds.
Serve with a lemon wedge and eat hot.

title: Elote – Grilled Corn on the Cob with Cashew-Lime Cream and Chilli
ingredients: Corn on the cob (pre-cooked, kernel weight)
instructions: Blend the cashews with 2 tbsp water, lime juice and salt into a smooth cream.
Brush the corn cobs with oil and grill on a barbecue or in a griddle pan for 8–10 minutes, turning, until charred in places.
Spread the hot cobs with the cashew cream.
Sprinkle with nutritional yeast, chilli powder and chopped coriander and serve with lime wedges.

title: Pkhali – Georgian Spinach and Walnut Balls with Pomegranate
ingredients: Utskho suneli (blue fenugreek), coriander seeds, salt
instructions: Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, refresh in cold water and squeeze out very thoroughly.
Grind the walnuts, garlic, spices and vinegar into a fine paste in a mini chopper.
Finely chop the spinach, coriander and onion, knead with the walnut paste and season with salt.
Shape into small balls, press a hollow into each with your thumb and fill with pomegranate seeds.
Serve with rye bread.

title: Matcha Latte with Soy Milk and Maple Syrup
instructions: Sift the matcha into a bowl and whisk with 50 ml hot but not boiling water (approx. 80°C) using a bamboo whisk until frothy.
Heat the soy drink and froth it.
Put the maple syrup into a large glass, pour in the matcha and top with the milk foam.

title: Strawberry Silken Tofu Smoothie with Oats
instructions: Wash and hull the strawberries, and break the banana into pieces.
Blend all the ingredients for 1 minute until very creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink immediately.

title: Soy Yoghurt with Pomegranate, Pistachios and Rose Water
instructions: Stir the soy yoghurt with a few drops of rose water and a pinch of cardamom until smooth.
Roughly chop the pistachios and finely dice the dates.
Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl and sprinkle with the pomegranate seeds, pistachios and dates.

title: Oven-Baked Kale Chips with Cashew and Nutritional Yeast Seasoning
ingredients: Smoked paprika, garlic powder, lemon juice, salt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 140°C (fan). Strip the kale from the stalks, tear into pieces, wash and spin very thoroughly dry.
Finely grind the cashews with the nutritional yeast, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Massage the kale with the olive oil and a little lemon juice and toss with the cashew seasoning.
Spread out on two lined baking trays and dry for 20–25 minutes until crisp, turning halfway through.

title: Puffed Quinoa Peanut Bars with Dark Chocolate
instructions: Finely chop the dates and stir with the peanut butter and maple syrup in a small pan over low heat until smooth.
Mix in the puffed quinoa, oats, chopped peanuts and salt.
Press the mixture firmly into a small lined tin and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate, drizzle over the top, leave to set and cut into 2 bars.

title: Tteokbokki with Tofu, White Cabbage and Spring Onions
instructions: If the rice cakes are hard, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes.
Bring the stock to the boil with the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic in a wide pan.
Add the rice cakes, cubed tofu and chopped white cabbage and simmer for 8–10 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Add the spring onion in pieces, cook for 1 minute and serve sprinkled with sesame seeds.

title: Mango Coconut Pudding with Agar-Agar and Lime
instructions: Finely purée 120 g mango with the coconut milk and maple syrup.
Stir the agar-agar into 50 ml water, bring to the boil and boil vigorously for 2 minutes.
Stir in the mango purée, heat briefly and pour into a glass or ramekin. Chill for at least 1 hour until set.
Serve with the soy yoghurt, the remaining mango diced, lime zest and mint.

title: Seed Crackers with Cucumber, Tomato and Cress
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Mix the seeds, oats and salt with the water and leave to swell for 15 minutes.
Spread the mixture very thinly on a lined baking tray and cut into pieces after 10 minutes of baking.
Bake for another 35–40 minutes until the crackers are dry and crisp, then leave to cool.
Top with cucumber and tomato slices, cress, salt and pepper.

title: Chickpea Almond Cookies with Dark Chocolate
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Rinse the chickpeas well and pat dry.
Process with the almond butter, maple syrup, oats, baking powder, vanilla and salt in a mini chopper into a smooth dough.
Chop the chocolate and fold it in.
Shape 3 cookies, flatten on baking paper and bake for 14 minutes. Leave to firm up on the tray.

title: Kedgeree – British Curry Rice with Smoked Haddock, Egg and Peas
instructions: Cook the basmati rice according to the packet instructions, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Poach the haddock in barely simmering water for 6 minutes, lift out and flake into large pieces.
Boil the egg for 8 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and quarter.
Finely dice the onion and soften in the oil for 4 minutes, then briefly toast the curry powder and turmeric with it.
Fold in the rice, peas and fish, season with lemon juice and pepper and serve with the egg and parsley.

title: Mackerel in Tomato Sauce on Crispbread with Egg, Cucumber and Dill
instructions: Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes, cool, peel and slice.
Spread the crispbread thinly with cream cheese.
Roughly break up the mackerel with a little of its tomato sauce using a fork and spread over two slices.
Top the remaining slices with cucumber and egg, then sprinkle everything with dill and pepper.

title: Wholegrain English Muffin with Fried Egg, Turkey Breast, Tomato and Spinach
instructions: Split the English muffin and toast it golden in the toaster.
Fry the egg in a greased metal ring in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Briefly warm the turkey breast in the pan.
Layer the bottom half with spinach, turkey, tomato slices, cheese and the fried egg and cover with the top half.

title: Kuku Sabzi – Persian Herb Omelette with Walnuts, Yoghurt and Flatbread
instructions: Chop the herbs very finely and roughly break up the walnuts.
Whisk the eggs with the flour, turmeric, baking powder, salt and pepper, then stir in the herbs and walnuts.
Pour the mixture into a small non-stick pan with the hot oil and let it set, covered, over low heat for 10 minutes.
Flip the kuku with the help of a plate and fry for another 3 minutes.
Cut into pieces and serve with yoghurt and warm flatbread.

title: Mangú – Dominican Plantain Mash with Fried Egg, Red Onions and Grilling Cheese
instructions: Peel the plantain, cut into pieces and boil in salted water for 15 minutes until soft.
Slice the red onion into rings and sweat in 3 g oil for 3 minutes, deglaze with the vinegar and set aside.
Drain the plantain, reserving some cooking water, and mash with 3 tbsp of it into a smooth purée.
Slice the cheese and fry golden in the remaining oil, then fry the egg.
Serve the mash with the vinegar onions, cheese and fried egg.

title: Gyeran-jjim – Korean Steamed Egg with Rice and Spinach Namul
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Whisk the eggs smoothly with the stock and a pinch of salt and pour through a sieve into a small heatproof bowl.
Cover the bowl and steam in a pot over gently simmering water for 12 minutes until the egg is set and fluffy. Sprinkle with spring onion rings.
Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, rinse in cold water, squeeze well and mix with soy sauce, grated garlic, sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Serve the steamed egg with rice and spinach namul.

title: Pannukakku – Finnish Oven Pancake with Berries and Skyr
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C and melt the butter in a small baking dish in the oven.
Whisk the egg, milk, flour, sugar, cardamom, vanilla and salt into a smooth, thin batter.
Pour the batter into the hot dish and bake for 18–20 minutes until the pancake puffs up and the edges are golden brown.
Let cool briefly and serve with skyr and berries.

title: Savoury Oat Porridge with Fried Egg, Mushrooms, Spinach and Sesame
instructions: Bring the oats to the boil in the stock and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Slice the mushrooms and fry in half the oil for 4 minutes, add the spinach and let it wilt.
Fry an egg with a runny yolk in the remaining oil.
Season the porridge with soy sauce, transfer to a bowl and top with the mushrooms, spinach, fried egg, spring onion, sesame and chilli flakes.

title: Sweet Potato Toast with Peanut Butter, Banana and Hemp Seeds
instructions: Wash the sweet potato thoroughly and cut lengthwise into 1 cm thick slices.
Toast the slices in the toaster on the highest setting for 2–3 rounds or roast in the oven at 200°C for 18 minutes until soft inside.
Spread with peanut butter while still warm and top with banana slices.
Finish with hemp seeds, cinnamon and maple syrup.

title: Teff Porridge with Pear, Cardamom and Pistachios
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with the water, soy drink, cardamom and a pinch of salt.
Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Meanwhile dice the pear and roughly chop the pistachios.
Sweeten the porridge with maple syrup and serve with pear, pistachios and cinnamon.

title: Overnight Kefir Buckwheat with Sour Cherries, Cocoa and Walnuts
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat thoroughly in a sieve.
Stir together with the kefir in a screw-top jar and leave to soak in the fridge overnight.
In the morning stir in the cocoa and honey.
Top with sour cherries and chopped walnuts.

title: Warm Quinoa Breakfast with Plums, Cinnamon and Almonds
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under hot water.
Bring to the boil with the soy drink, cinnamon and vanilla and leave to swell, covered, over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stone and quarter the plums and cook half of them along for the last 3 minutes.
Sweeten with maple syrup and serve with the remaining plums and chopped almonds.

title: Sabich – Israeli Pita with Aubergine, Egg, Tahini and Salad
instructions: Cut the aubergine into 1 cm thick slices, salt, brush with oil and fry in a pan for 4 minutes per side until soft and golden.
Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes, cool, peel and slice.
Finely dice the tomato, cucumber and parsley and mix with a little lemon juice and salt.
Stir the tahini with the remaining lemon juice and 1–2 tbsp water until creamy.
Open the pita, fill with aubergine, egg and salad and drizzle with tahini.

title: Turkey Breakfast Patties with Apple and Sage, Fried Egg and Roasted Tomatoes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roast the cherry tomatoes on a tray with salt and thyme for 15 minutes.
Knead the turkey mince with the apple, oats, chopped sage, salt and pepper and shape into 3 flat patties.
Fry the patties in 4 g oil for 4 minutes per side until cooked through.
Fry the egg in the remaining oil and serve everything with the tomatoes and toasted bread.

title: Poppy Seed Lemon Quark Cream with Berries and Spelt Flakes
instructions: Stir the quark with the milk, poppy seeds, lemon juice, zest and maple syrup until creamy and leave to infuse for 5 minutes.
Toast the spelt flakes in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until golden.
Spoon the quark cream into a bowl and top with berries and the toasted flakes.

title: Air Fryer Tuna Potato Cakes with Lime Yoghurt Dip
ingredients: Tuna (tinned in its own juice, drained)
instructions: Roughly mash the potatoes and mix with the tuna, egg, spring onion, salt and pepper into a mouldable mixture.
Shape 4 flat cakes, coat in panko and brush with the oil.
Bake in the air fryer at 190°C for 12 minutes until golden, turning halfway.
Stir the yoghurt with lime juice, zest, dill and salt and serve with the cakes.

title: Chamchi Gimbap – Korean Rice Rolls with Tuna, Egg and Spinach
ingredients: Tuna (tinned in its own juice, drained)
instructions: Cook the rice and, while still warm, mix with half the sesame oil and a little salt.
Whisk the egg and fry in the rapeseed oil into a thin omelette, then cut into strips. Briefly blanch and squeeze the spinach, cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks.
Stir the tuna with the yoghurt.
Spread a thin layer of rice on each nori sheet, lay the filling in a line on top and roll up tightly.
Brush the rolls with the remaining sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame and slice with a sharp, damp knife.

title: Air Fryer Onion Bhajis with Coriander Soy Yoghurt Dip
ingredients: Cumin, turmeric, chilli, baking powder, salt
instructions: Cut the onions into thin half rings, salt and leave for 10 minutes.
Add the chickpea flour, grated ginger, spices and 2–3 tbsp water until a thick batter coats the onions.
Form 6 loose heaps, place on baking paper in the air fryer, drizzle with the oil and bake at 190°C for 12 minutes until crisp, turning halfway.
Stir the soy yoghurt with chopped coriander and salt and serve alongside.

title: Air Fryer Okra Chips with Chaat Masala and Lime Yoghurt
instructions: Wash the okra, pat very dry and halve lengthwise.
Toss with the oil, chickpea flour, chilli and salt until every pod is thinly coated.
Bake in the air fryer at 190°C for 12–14 minutes until crisp, shaking twice.
Season with chaat masala and lime juice. Stir the yoghurt with salt and a little lime and serve alongside.

title: Oven Beef Jerky with Pepper, Garlic and Soy Sauce
instructions: Freeze the beef for 30 minutes, then cut across the grain into 3–4 mm thin strips.
Stir together the soy sauce, maple syrup, paprika and garlic powder and marinate the meat in it in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Pat the strips dry, sprinkle with coarse pepper and lay them side by side on an oven rack.
Dry at 75°C fan with a wooden spoon wedged in the oven door for 3–4 hours until the jerky is pliable but dry. Store airtight.

title: Yakitori Negima – Chicken and Leek Skewers with Soy Glaze
instructions: Soak wooden skewers for 15 minutes. Cut the chicken into 3 cm pieces and the leek into 3 cm lengths.
Thread alternately onto 4 skewers and brush with the oil.
Reduce the soy sauce, maple syrup and grated ginger in a pan for 2 minutes into a thick glaze.
Cook the skewers in a grill pan or under the oven grill for 10–12 minutes, turning, brushing twice with glaze during the last minutes, and sprinkle with shichimi.

title: Air Fryer Quark Balls with Cinnamon Sugar
instructions: Stir the quark, egg, 7 g sugar, vanilla and salt until smooth, then briefly knead in the flour and baking powder.
With lightly oiled hands shape 8 balls and brush thinly with oil.
Bake on baking paper in the air fryer at 170°C for 10–12 minutes until golden.
Mix the remaining sugar with cinnamon and roll the warm balls in it.

title: Air Fryer Samosas with Potato and Pea Filling and Mint Dip
instructions: Peel and dice the potatoes and boil for 10 minutes until soft, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Finely chop the onion and ginger, sweat in 2 g oil, add the spices, potatoes and peas and roughly mash.
Cut each filo sheet lengthwise into 2 strips, brush with the remaining oil, place 1 tbsp filling on each and fold into triangles.
Bake in the air fryer at 180°C for 10 minutes until golden.
Stir the soy yoghurt with chopped mint and salt and serve alongside.

title: Mini Peppers Stuffed with Herb Cottage Cheese and Pumpkin Seeds
instructions: Halve the mini peppers lengthwise and remove the seeds.
Stir the cottage cheese with chopped herbs, finely grated garlic, salt and pepper.
Fill the pepper halves with the cream.
Briefly toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan and sprinkle over with chilli flakes.

title: Air Fryer Empanadas with Black Beans, Corn and Cheese
instructions: Roughly mash the beans and mix with the corn, finely diced pepper and onion, cheese, cumin, paprika and salt.
Place the filling on one half of each tortilla, fold over and press the edges firmly with a fork.
Brush with the oil and bake in the air fryer at 190°C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Finely dice the tomato, mix with lime juice, coriander and salt and serve as a salsa.

title: Zacuscă – Romanian Aubergine and Pepper Spread with Rye Bread
instructions: Roast the aubergine and pepper in the oven at 230°C for 25 minutes until the skin blisters black. Rest briefly, covered, then peel.
Finely dice the onion and soften in the oil for 5 minutes.
Finely chop the aubergine and pepper, add to the onion with the tomato paste and bay leaf and cook down for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, let cool and serve on rye bread.

title: Stuffed Dates with Almond Butter, Dark Chocolate and Sea Salt
instructions: Slit the dates lengthwise and remove the stones.
Fill with almond butter.
Melt the chocolate over a water bath, drizzle over the dates and sprinkle with a pinch of sea salt.
Chill for 10 minutes until the chocolate has set.

title: Zi Ran Yang Rou – Cumin Lamb with Peppers, Onions and Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Cut the lamb into thin strips and mix with soy sauce and cornflour.
Toast the cumin in a dry pan for 1 minute and coarsely crush.
Sear the lamb in the hot oil in a wok for 2–3 minutes and remove.
Stir-fry the onion and pepper strips with the garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the lamb, cumin and chilli flakes, toss for 1 minute and serve with coriander and rice.

title: Kabab Koobideh – Persian Minced Lamb Skewers with Saffron Rice and Grilled Tomato
instructions: Cook the basmati rice. Steep a few saffron threads in 2 tbsp hot water and mix into part of the rice with the butter.
Knead the minced lamb vigorously with the grated onion, turmeric, salt and pepper for 3 minutes until sticky.
Press the mixture into 2 long, flat kebabs around wide metal skewers.
Cook the skewers with the halved tomatoes in a grill pan or under the oven grill for 8–10 minutes, turning several times.
Serve with saffron rice, tomatoes, fresh herbs and sumac.

title: Venison Medallions with Chanterelles, Brussels Sprouts, Lingonberries and Sweet Potato Mash
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potatoes and boil in salted water for 15 minutes until soft. Halve the Brussels sprouts and steam for 7 minutes.
Season the medallions with salt and pepper and fry in the oil with thyme and juniper for 2–3 minutes per side until pink, then rest in foil.
In the pan juices, fry the shallot and chanterelles briskly for 4 minutes and season.
Drain the sweet potatoes and purée finely with butter, nutmeg and 2 tbsp cooking water.
Plate the medallions with chanterelles, Brussels sprouts, mash and lingonberries.

title: Pink Duck Breast with Orange Fennel Salad and Couscous
instructions: Pour 75 ml boiling salted water over the couscous and leave to swell, covered, for 5 minutes.
Season the duck breast with salt and pepper, fry in 3 g oil for 4 minutes per side, glaze with honey and rest for 5 minutes.
Shave the fennel wafer-thin. Peel and segment the orange, catching the juice.
Toss the fennel, orange segments and rocket with the orange juice, remaining olive oil, salt and pepper.
Slice the duck and serve with the salad and fluffed couscous.

title: Fiskekaker – Norwegian Fish Cakes with Peas, Carrots and Potatoes
instructions: Peel and halve the potatoes and cook in salted water for 18 minutes. Slice the carrots and steam with the peas for 6 minutes.
Cut the pollock into pieces and blend with the egg, starch, milk, onion, salt and nutmeg into a smooth mixture.
With wet hands shape 4 flat cakes.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
Serve with potatoes, peas, carrots and chives.

title: Chả Cá – Vietnamese Turmeric Fish with Dill, Rice Noodles and Peanuts
instructions: Cut the fish into 4 cm pieces and marinate with turmeric, garlic and half the fish sauce for 10 minutes.
Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet instructions and drain.
Fry the fish in the oil for 3 minutes per side until golden yellow.
Add the dill in large sprigs and the spring onions in pieces and fry for 1 minute until wilted.
Serve with rice noodles, lettuce, chopped peanuts, chilli and lime and drizzle with the remaining fish sauce.

title: Ojingeo Bokkeum – Spicy Stir-Fried Squid with Vegetables and Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Score the inside of the squid in a crosshatch and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, garlic, gochugaru and sesame oil into a sauce.
Cut the onion, carrot, courgette and cabbage into strips and stir-fry briskly in the rapeseed oil in a wok for 3 minutes.
Add the squid and sauce and stir-fry for just 2–3 minutes until just cooked.
Sprinkle with sesame and serve with rice.

title: Baja-Style Fish Tacos with Red Cabbage, Avocado and Lime Yoghurt
instructions: Shave the red cabbage very finely and knead with a little lime juice and salt.
Season the fish with paprika, cumin, chilli and salt, fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side, then break into large pieces.
Stir the yoghurt with the remaining lime juice and salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and top with red cabbage, fish, avocado slices, lime yoghurt and coriander.

title: Piri Piri Prawns with Lemon Rice and Tomato Salad
instructions: Cook the rice and mix with the lemon zest and some of the juice.
Pound the chilli, garlic, paprika, oregano, salt, 5 g oil and the remaining lemon juice into a paste and marinate the prawns in it for 10 minutes.
Cut the tomatoes and red onion into wedges and mix with coriander and salt.
Fry the prawns in the remaining oil in a hot pan for 1–2 minutes per side until pink.
Serve with the lemon rice and tomato salad.

title: Sopa de Albóndigas – Mexican Meatball Soup with Vegetables
instructions: Knead the mince with 10 g uncooked rice, chopped mint, cumin and salt and shape into 8 small balls.
Dice the onion and bring to the boil with the passata, stock, oregano and chipotle.
Dice the carrot and potato, add to the soup with the remaining rice and the meatballs and simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Dice the courgette, cook it along for the last 5 minutes and serve the soup with coriander.

title: Shiro Wot – Ethiopian Chickpea Stew with Gomen and Injera
instructions: Chop the onion very finely and dry-roast for 5 minutes, then add 7 g oil, the garlic, berbere and diced tomato and braise for 3 minutes.
Gradually stir in the chickpea flour with the water until smooth.
Simmer for 12–15 minutes, stirring constantly, until a thick, glossy stew forms. Season with salt.
Roughly chop the spinach and sauté in the remaining oil with ginger and salt for 3 minutes.
Serve the shiro and gomen on injera.

title: Tacu Tacu – Peruvian Bean and Rice Cake with Fried Egg and Salsa Criolla
instructions: Cook the rice. Slice the red onion thinly, mix with lime juice, chilli, coriander and salt and leave to marinate as salsa criolla.
Finely chop the onion and garlic and sweat in 3 g oil for 3 minutes.
Roughly mash the beans, combine with the rice, onions, oregano, salt and pepper and shape into an oblong cake.
Fry the cake in the remaining oil for 4 minutes per side until crisp, then fry the egg.
Serve the tacu tacu with the fried egg, tomato wedges and salsa criolla.

title: Sundubu Jjigae – Korean Silken Tofu Stew with Egg, Courgette and Rice
instructions: Cook the rice. Chop the onion and garlic and sweat in the sesame oil with gochugaru for 1 minute.
Add the stock, gochujang and soy sauce and simmer the sliced shiitake and diced courgette in it for 5 minutes.
Spoon the silken tofu into the pot in large pieces and let it steep gently for 4 minutes.
Crack the egg into the centre, let it set for 2 minutes and sprinkle with spring onion.
Serve bubbling hot with the rice.

title: Vinegret – Russian Beetroot Salad with Beans, Sauerkraut and Rye Bread
instructions: Cut the beetroot, potatoes, carrot and gherkin into 1 cm cubes.
Toss the beetroot with 3 g oil first so it does not stain the other ingredients too much.
Mix all the diced vegetables with the beans, squeezed sauerkraut and finely chopped onion.
Dress with the remaining oil, salt, pepper and dill and serve with rye bread.

title: Adas Polo – Persian Lentil Rice with Dates, Raisins and Cucumber Soy Yoghurt
ingredients: Saffron, cinnamon, cumin, dried mint, salt
instructions: Cook the lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until al dente, cooking the rice at the same time.
Slice the onion into thin rings and fry in 6 g oil for 10 minutes until golden. Toast the dates, raisins and almonds with cinnamon in the remaining oil for 2 minutes.
Mix the lentils and rice with cumin and saffron dissolved in a little warm water.
Finely grate the cucumber and stir with the soy yoghurt, mint and salt.
Serve the lentil rice with the crispy onions, the date and raisin mixture and the cucumber yoghurt.

title: Cottage Cheese Cookie Dough with Chocolate Chunks
instructions: Blend the cottage cheese in a blender or with a stick blender until completely smooth.
Stir in the peanut butter, maple syrup, vanilla and salt.
Grind the oats finely and work them in until a thick cookie dough forms.
Roughly chop the chocolate, fold in and chill the dough for 15 minutes, then spoon straight from the jar.

title: Cold Brew Protein Ice Cream with Skyr and Vanilla
instructions: Stir the skyr, milk, cold brew, protein powder and maple syrup until smooth.
Pour into a freezer-safe tub and freeze for at least 24 hours.
Process until creamy in an ice cream maker with a pacotizing function, or let thaw for 10 minutes and blend until creamy with a stick blender.
Dust with cocoa and serve immediately.

title: Watermelon Lime Sorbet with Mint
instructions: Cut the watermelon into cubes and freeze on a board for at least 4 hours.
Blend the frozen cubes with the lime juice, zest and maple syrup in a high-speed blender into a creamy sorbet.
Serve immediately with mint, or freeze for another 30 minutes and then scoop.

title: Proffee – Protein Iced Coffee Shake with Date and Cinnamon
instructions: Brew the espresso and let it cool.
Blend the milk, protein powder, date and cinnamon until very smooth and frothy.
Fill a large glass with ice cubes, pour in the shake and slowly pour the espresso over the top.

title: Fibermaxxing Bowl with Oat Bran, Skyr, Raspberries, Kiwi and Flaxseed
instructions: Stir the oat bran with the milk and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Stir in the skyr and transfer to a bowl.
Peel the kiwi and slice.
Top with raspberries, kiwi and flaxseed and drizzle with honey.

title: Fibermaxxing Legume Salad with Pearl Barley, Artichokes and Mustard Lemon Dressing
instructions: Cook the barley in salted water for 20 minutes until al dente, drain and rinse cold. Add the edamame for the last 4 minutes.
Rinse the kidney beans and chickpeas, quarter the artichokes and finely dice the red onion.
Whisk the olive oil, mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Mix everything with parsley and the dressing and serve with rocket. Keeps well in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Cherry Cocoa Shake with Cottage Cheese and Banana
instructions: Put all the ingredients into the blender.
Blend on the highest setting for 1 minute until the shake is completely smooth and creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink immediately.

title: Vegan Chocolate Tahini Pudding from Silken Tofu with Orange and Sesame
instructions: Drain the silken tofu and blend with the cocoa, tahini, maple syrup, vanilla and salt until completely smooth.
Pour into a glass and chill for at least 30 minutes so the pudding firms up.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden. Segment the orange.
Serve the pudding with the orange segments and sesame.

title: Etli Yeşil Fasulye (Green Beans with Beef) and Yoghurt
instructions: Brown the beef well on all sides in the olive oil in a casserole.
Add the diced onion and fry for 4 minutes, then briefly toast the tomato and pepper pastes.
Trim the beans, halve them and add to the pot along with the tomatoes and water.
Cover and braise over low heat for 35 minutes until the meat and beans are tender, then season with salt, pepper and pul biber.
Serve with yoghurt.

title: Etli Nohut (Chickpea Stew with Beef) with Bulgur Pilaf
instructions: Brown the beef in the oil in a casserole, add the diced onion and sweat until translucent.
Stir in the tomato and pepper pastes and toast briefly.
Add the chickpeas and water, cover and braise over low heat for 35 minutes until the meat is tender.
Soak the bulgur in twice its volume of salted water for 10 minutes and fluff it up.
Season the etli nohut with salt, pepper and cumin and serve with the bulgur.

title: Etli Türlü (Braised Vegetable Pot with Lamb)
instructions: Brown the lamb in the oil in a wide pot, add the onion and sweat for 4 minutes.
Cut the aubergine, courgette, potato and pepper into large chunks and halve the beans.
Layer the vegetables over the meat, pour over the tomatoes and water and season with salt.
Cover and braise over low heat for 40 minutes without stirring until everything is tender.
Season with pepper and thyme and serve warm.

title: Karnıyarık (Stuffed Aubergines with Minced Beef) and Rice
instructions: Peel the aubergines lengthwise in stripes, brush with oil and bake at 220 °C for 20 minutes until soft.
Fry the mince until crumbly, add the onion and pepper and fry for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and half of the diced tomato.
Slit the aubergines lengthwise, press them open, fill with the mince mixture and top with the remaining tomato slices.
Bake in the dish with a little water for another 15 minutes.
Cook the rice and serve with the aubergines, sprinkled with parsley.

title: İzmir Köfte (Oven Köfte with Potatoes, Peppers and Tomato Sauce)
instructions: Knead the mince with the grated onion, breadcrumbs, parsley, cumin, salt and pepper and shape into oblong köfte.
Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with half of the oil and spread out in a baking dish with the köfte.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Stir the passata with a little water and the remaining oil, pour it over and tuck the peppers and tomato wedges in between.
Bake for another 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.

title: Hasanpaşa Köfte (Köfte Topped with Mashed Potato in Tomato Sauce)
instructions: Peel the potatoes, boil in salted water for 20 minutes until soft and mash with warm milk, butter and nutmeg into a firm purée.
Knead the mince with the onion, breadcrumbs, salt, pepper and cumin, shape into flat round köfte and press a hollow into the centre of each.
Place the köfte in a dish, pipe the purée into the hollows and sprinkle with kaşar.
Thin the passata with a little water and pour it around the köfte.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes until the cheese is golden brown.

title: Kadınbudu Köfte (Beef and Rice Köfte in an Egg Coating) with Salad
instructions: Boil the rice in salted water for 12 minutes until soft and drain.
Fry half of the mince with the finely diced onion until crumbly and leave to cool.
Knead the fried and raw mince with the rice, salt, pepper and cumin and shape into flat oval köfte.
Dredge the köfte in flour, dip in the beaten egg and fry in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve with tomatoes, cucumber, lettuce and lemon juice.

title: Tavuk Sote (Chicken Sauté with Peppers, Mushrooms and Tomatoes) with Bulgur
instructions: Soak the bulgur in twice its volume of salted water for 10 minutes.
Dice the chicken and sear in the hot oil for 5 minutes.
Add the onion, peppers and mushrooms and fry for 5 minutes.
Stir in the pepper paste and diced tomatoes, braise for 5 minutes and season with thyme, salt and pepper.
Serve with the bulgur.

title: Orman Kebabı (Lamb Stew with Peas, Carrots, Potatoes and Mushrooms)
instructions: Brown the lamb well in the oil in a casserole.
Add the diced onion, sweat until translucent and briefly toast the tomato paste.
Deglaze with water, cover and braise for 35 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and carrots and the mushrooms and cook for another 15 minutes.
Add the peas, leave to steep for 5 minutes and season with thyme, salt and pepper.

title: Tas Kebabı (Braised Beef) with Rice Pilaf
instructions: Brown the beef on all sides in the hot butter in a pot.
Finely dice the onions, add and sweat for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, add the diced tomato and water, cover and braise over low heat for 70 minutes until the meat is very tender.
Cook the rice, covered, in 1.5 times its volume of salted water for 15 minutes.
Arrange the tas kebabı next to the rice and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Hünkar Beğendi (Lamb Ragout on Aubergine Cheese Purée)
instructions: Brown the lamb in the oil, add the onion and sweat for 5 minutes, then add the tomato paste, diced tomato and a little water, cover and braise for 50 minutes.
Char the aubergines all over on a gas flame or under the grill, peel and chop finely.
Melt the butter, sweat the flour in it, gradually stir in the milk and simmer for 3 minutes to make a béchamel.
Stir in the aubergines and kaşar and season with salt and nutmeg.
Spread the purée on a plate and place the lamb ragout in the centre.

title: Mantı (Turkish Dumplings with Minced Beef, Garlic Yoghurt and Paprika Butter)
instructions: Knead the flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt into a firm dough and leave to rest for 20 minutes.
Mix the mince with the onion, salt and pepper. Roll the dough out very thinly and cut into 3 cm squares.
Place a small ball of filling on each and pinch the corners together into little parcels.
Boil the mantı in plenty of salted water for 10 minutes. Stir the yoghurt with the grated garlic.
Arrange the drained mantı with the garlic yoghurt and drizzle with paprika, pul biber and mint heated in butter.

title: Levrek Buğulama (Steamed Sea Bass with Tomatoes and Potatoes)
instructions: Slice the potatoes thinly and parboil in salted water for 8 minutes.
Cut the onion, pepper and garlic into strips and sweat in the oil in a wide pan for 4 minutes.
Spread the potatoes and tomato slices on top, lay the salted fish over them and pour in the water.
Cover and steam over low heat for 12 minutes until the fish is cooked.
Drizzle with lemon juice, sprinkle with herbs and serve immediately.

title: Çökertme Kebabı (Beef Strips on Oven Potato Straws with Garlic Yoghurt)
instructions: Cut the potatoes into very fine matchsticks, toss with 6 g oil and bake at 220 °C for 25 minutes until crisp, turning once.
Stir the yoghurt with grated garlic and salt.
Slice the steak into thin strips and sear with the pepper in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, then briefly stir in the tomato paste and a splash of water.
Place the potato straws on a plate, spread the yoghurt over them and arrange the meat and pepper on top.
Brown the butter and drizzle it over the meat.

title: Tantuni (Beef Wrap from Mersin with Tomatoes, Onions and Parsley)
instructions: Cut the beef into very fine strips.
Fry the meat in the oil in a hot pan for 3 minutes, deglaze with a splash of water and season with pul biber, salt and cumin.
Slice the onion into fine rings and mix with sumac and parsley. Dice the tomato.
Warm the lavash briefly in the pan, fill with the meat, tomato and onions, drizzle with lemon juice and roll up tightly.

title: Tavuk Döner Bowl (Chicken Döner with Bulgur, Salad and Garlic Yoghurt)
ingredients: Greek yoghurt (0.2% fat, for marinade and sauce)
instructions: Cut the chicken into thin strips and marinate for 15 minutes with 30 g yoghurt, the pepper paste, oil, cumin, paprika and salt.
Soak the bulgur in twice its volume of salted water for 10 minutes.
Fry the chicken in a hot pan for 6 minutes until browned and crispy at the edges.
Stir the remaining yoghurt with garlic. Finely slice the red cabbage, tomato, cucumber and onion.
Arrange the bulgur, salad and chicken in a bowl and serve with the garlic yoghurt.

title: Kuşbaşılı Pide (Boat-Shaped Flatbread with Diced Beef, Tomato and Pepper)
instructions: Knead the flour, yeast, salt, lukewarm water and oil into a smooth dough and leave to rise for 60 minutes.
Cut the beef into very small cubes and mix with the diced tomato, pepper, onion, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough into a long oval, spread the filling on top, fold in the edges and pinch the ends together into a boat shape.
Brush the edges with egg, sprinkle the kaşar over the filling and bake at 240 °C for 12 to 14 minutes.

title: Balık Ekmek (Mackerel Sandwich with Sumac Onions and Salad)
instructions: Salt the mackerel fillets and fry in a grill pan with the oil for 4 minutes skin side down, then 2 minutes on the other side.
Slice the onion into fine rings and mix with sumac and salt.
Cut open the bread and toast briefly in the pan.
Fill with lettuce, tomato slices, fish and onions and drizzle with lemon juice.

title: Nohutlu Tavuklu Pilav (Istanbul-Style Rice with Chicken and Chickpeas)
instructions: Poach the chicken in lightly salted water for 20 minutes, lift out and shred, then measure out 150 ml of the stock.
Wash the rice, toast it in the butter for 2 minutes and add the chickpeas and stock.
Cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, then leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Arrange the rice with the chicken, sprinkle with pepper and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Düğün Çorbası (Wedding Soup with Lamb, Yoghurt and Lemon)
instructions: Bring the lamb to the boil with the water and a little salt, skim, cover and simmer for 50 minutes until tender, then lift out and shred.
Whisk the yoghurt, egg yolk, flour and lemon juice until smooth and temper with a ladle of hot stock.
Pour the mixture into the stock while stirring and simmer gently for 5 minutes without letting it bubble.
Return the meat, drizzle the soup with paprika sizzled in butter and serve with bread.

title: İskender Kebap Light (Beef on Flatbread with Tomato Sauce and Yoghurt)
instructions: Slice the steak wafer-thin, salt it and fry in batches in a very hot pan for 1 minute. Briefly fry the pepper and tomato too.
Simmer the passata with 3 g butter and salt for 5 minutes.
Cube the flatbread, spread it on a plate and drizzle with half of the tomato sauce.
Layer the meat on top, pour over the remaining sauce and add the yoghurt alongside.
Brown the remaining butter, pour it over the meat and serve with the pepper and tomato.

title: Kuzu Şiş (Lamb Skewers with Tomato Bulgur and Sumac Onions)
instructions: Cut the lamb into 3 cm cubes and marinate for at least 30 minutes with the oil, the juice of half a grated onion, thyme, pul biber and salt.
Thread the meat onto skewers, alternating with pieces of pepper.
Soak the bulgur with the diced tomato in twice its volume of salted water for 10 minutes.
Cook the skewers on the grill or in a grill pan for 8 to 10 minutes, turning all round.
Slice the remaining onion into rings, mix with sumac and parsley and serve with the bulgur and cucumber slices alongside the skewers.

title: Fırın Kuzu Tandır Light (Slow-Cooked Lamb with Roast Potatoes and Salad)
ingredients: Leg of lamb (lean, in one piece)
instructions: Rub the leg of lamb with salt, cumin and thyme and place it in a roasting tin with onion rings, garlic and a glass of water.
Cover and cook at 150 °C for 2.5 hours until the meat can be pulled apart with a fork.
Quarter the potatoes, toss with the oil and place them next to the meat for the last hour, then brown uncovered for 15 minutes at the end.
Pull the meat apart and serve with the potatoes and a tomato-cucumber salad.

title: Keşkek (Wheat and Chicken Porridge with Paprika Butter)
instructions: Soak the wheat overnight, drain and bring to the boil with the chicken, water and salt.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 90 minutes until the wheat is very soft, adding water if needed.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot.
Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until a thick, creamy mass forms.
Heat the butter with the paprika and drizzle it over the keşkek.

title: Çerkez Tavuğu (Circassian Chicken in Walnut Sauce) with Bread
instructions: Poach the chicken in lightly salted water for 20 minutes, leave to cool and shred finely, reserving 100 ml of the stock.
Soak the toast bread in a little stock and blend with the walnuts, garlic and salt into a creamy sauce, adding more stock if needed.
Mix the chicken with two thirds of the sauce, arrange on lettuce leaves and spread the remaining sauce on top.
Stir the oil with the paprika, drizzle over and serve with bread.

title: Ankara Tava (Lamb with Oven-Baked Arpa Şehriye Pilaf)
instructions: Braise the lamb with the onion, salt and 250 ml water, covered, for 45 minutes until tender.
Toast the arpa şehriye in the butter until golden and briefly toast the tomato and pepper pastes with it.
Put the pasta, the lamb with its braising liquid, the diced tomato and the remaining water into a baking dish and season with thyme and pepper.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the top turns slightly crispy.

title: Elbasan Tava (Oven-Baked Lamb in a Yoghurt-Egg Crust)
instructions: Brown the lamb in the butter, braise covered with a little water and thyme for 35 minutes until tender and transfer to a small baking dish.
Stir the flour into the milk until smooth and bring briefly to the boil until the mixture thickens, then leave to cool slightly.
Stir in the yoghurt, egg, salt and nutmeg and pour the cream over the meat.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes until the crust has set and is speckled golden brown.
Serve with tomato slices and bread.

title: Kuru Fasulye (White Bean Stew in Tomato-Pepper Sauce) with Rice Pilaf
instructions: Dice the onion and pointed pepper and sweat in the olive oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the pepper and tomato pastes and toast for 1 minute.
Add the beans and stock, simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until thick and season with salt, pepper and pul biber.
Wash the rice and cook, covered, in twice its volume of salted water for 15 minutes, then leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Serve the beans with the rice.

title: İmam Bayıldı (Braised Aubergines with Onion-Tomato Filling) with Flatbread
instructions: Peel the aubergines in stripes, soak in salted water for 15 minutes, pat dry and roast with 10 g oil at 220 °C for 20 minutes.
Slice the onions into half rings and sweat slowly with the garlic in the remaining oil for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the diced tomatoes, sugar and parsley and reduce for 5 minutes.
Slit the aubergines lengthwise, fill with the onion mixture and braise covered with a little water at 180 °C for 20 minutes.
Serve lukewarm or cold with flatbread.

title: Zeytinyağlı Bezelye (Peas with Carrots and Potatoes in Olive Oil)
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the olive oil for 4 minutes until translucent.
Cut the carrot and potato into small cubes and sweat for 3 minutes.
Add the peas, sugar, salt and water, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Fold in the dill, leave to cool until lukewarm and serve with bread.

title: Ispanak Yemeği (Spinach and Rice Pot) with Garlic Yoghurt
instructions: Dice the onion, sweat in the oil for 4 minutes and briefly toast the tomato paste.
Add the washed rice and the water and simmer for 5 minutes.
Gradually fold in the roughly chopped spinach, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir the yoghurt with the grated garlic and a little salt and serve with the spinach.

title: Zeytinyağlı Pırasa (Leeks with Carrots and Rice in Olive Oil)
instructions: Trim the leek, halve lengthwise and cut into 2 cm pieces. Slice the carrot.
Sweat the carrot in the olive oil for 3 minutes, then add the leek and sweat for 5 minutes.
Add the washed rice, sugar, salt and water, cover and cook over low heat for 25 minutes.
Drizzle with lemon juice, leave to cool and serve lukewarm or cold with bread.

title: Nohutlu Kabak Yemeği (Courgette and Chickpea Pot with Dill and Yoghurt)
instructions: Dice the onion, sweat in the oil for 3 minutes and briefly toast the tomato paste.
Cut the courgette into half slices, dice the tomatoes and add both with the chickpeas.
Cover and braise for 15 minutes until the courgette is soft but not falling apart.
Season with dill, salt and pepper and serve with yoghurt.

title: Fellah Köftesi (Bulgur Dumplings in Tomato-Garlic Sauce)
instructions: Pour 100 ml hot water over the bulgur and leave to swell for 15 minutes.
Knead the bulgur vigorously with the semolina, flour, 5 g pepper paste and salt for 5 minutes into a pliable dough and shape into small dumplings with a thumb hollow.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 8 minutes until they float and drain.
Sweat the garlic in the oil, stir in the remaining pepper and tomato pastes, the lemon juice and 150 ml cooking water and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss the dumplings in the sauce and serve with parsley.

title: Patlıcanlı Pilav (Aubergine Rice with Chickpeas and Mint)
instructions: Dice the aubergine, salt it, leave for 10 minutes, pat dry and roast with 8 g oil at 220 °C for 20 minutes.
Dice the onion and sweat in the remaining oil, dice the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the washed rice, chickpeas and 140 ml water, season with salt, cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Fold in the aubergines, leave to rest for 10 minutes and sprinkle with mint.

title: İç Pilav (Spiced Rice with Pine Nuts and Currants) with Yoghurt
instructions: Finely dice the onion and toast with the pine nuts in the oil until golden brown.
Wash the rice, add and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the currants, cinnamon, allspice, salt and 140 ml hot water, cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Fold in the dill, leave to rest for 10 minutes and serve with yoghurt and tomato slices.

title: Zeytinyağlı Enginar (Artichoke Bottoms with Peas, Carrots and Dill) with Bulgur
instructions: Whisk the lemon juice with the flour and water until smooth.
Chop the spring onions and carrot and sweat in the olive oil for 5 minutes, then add the peas and salt.
Place the artichoke bottoms on top, hollow side up, pour over the lemon water, cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Pour twice its volume of boiling salted water over the bulgur and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Leave the artichokes to cool in their liquid, fill the bottoms with the vegetables, sprinkle with dill and serve with bulgur.

title: Zeytinyağlı Kereviz (Celeriac with Orange, Carrots and Peas)
instructions: Peel the celeriac, dice and drizzle immediately with lemon juice.
Dice the carrot and sweat in the olive oil for 3 minutes.
Add the celeriac, orange juice, sugar, salt and water, cover and cook for 25 minutes until tender.
Add the peas for the last 5 minutes, leave to cool, sprinkle with dill and serve with bread.

title: Mantar Güveç (Mushrooms with Peppers and Kaşar from the Clay Pot)
instructions: Quarter the mushrooms, slice the pepper into rings and dice the tomato.
Sear the mushrooms in the hot oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic, pepper and tomato, fry for 3 minutes and season with thyme and salt.
Transfer to a small ovenproof clay dish and sprinkle with kaşar.
Bake at 220 °C for 8 minutes until the cheese bubbles and serve with flatbread.

title: Zeytinyağlı Bakla (Broad Beans with Dill) and Garlic Yoghurt
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the oil for 3 minutes.
Add the broad beans, sugar, salt and water, cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Mix with lemon juice and plenty of dill and leave to cool.
Stir the yoghurt with garlic and serve with the beans and bread.

title: Kumpir (Baked Potato with Kaşar, Sweetcorn, Peas, Olives and Red Cabbage)
instructions: Wash the potato, prick several times and bake at 200 °C for 60 minutes until completely soft inside.
Cut open lengthwise, fluff the inside with a fork and mix with butter, salt and kaşar until the cheese melts.
Top with sweetcorn, peas, olives, red cabbage and yoghurt and serve immediately.

title: Ispanaklı Yumurtalı Pide (Pide with Spinach, Kaşar and Egg)
instructions: Knead the flour, yeast, salt, lukewarm water and oil and leave to rise for 60 minutes.
Wilt the spinach with chopped garlic in a pan, squeeze out well, season with pepper and mix with the grated kaşar.
Roll the dough into an oval, place the filling in the centre and fold the edges into a boat shape.
Bake at 240 °C for 8 minutes, then slide the egg into the centre and bake for another 5 minutes until the white has set.

title: Patatesli Gözleme (Flatbread with Potato, Kaşar and Parsley)
instructions: Knead the flour, water and salt into a soft dough and leave to rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the potato, mash and mix with finely chopped onion, parsley, pul biber and salt.
Roll the dough out wafer-thin into a circle, cover one half with the potato mixture and kaşar and fold over.
Cook in a hot dry pan for 3 minutes per side, brush with butter and cut into pieces.

title: Air Fryer Sigara Böreği (Crispy Filo Rolls with White Cheese and Parsley)
instructions: Crumble the feta and mix with finely chopped parsley and half of the egg.
Cut the filo into triangles, place a strip of filling along the wide side, fold in the sides and roll up tightly into cigars, sealing the tip with egg.
Brush the rolls with oil and air-fry at 190 °C for 8 minutes until golden brown.
Serve with cucumber and tomato.

title: Mıhlama (Kuymak – Cornmeal and Cheese Skillet from the Black Sea Region)
instructions: Melt the butter in a small pan and toast the cornmeal in it for 2 minutes.
Gradually stir in the water and simmer for 3 minutes while stirring.
Stir in the kaşar and let it melt over low heat without stirring until it forms cheesy strings.
Eat straight from the pan with bread, cucumber and tomato.

title: Simit (Turkish Sesame Ring) with White Cheese, Tomato, Cucumber and Olives
instructions: Knead the flour, yeast, salt and lukewarm water into a firm dough and leave to rise for 45 minutes.
Roll the dough into two strands, twist into a rope and close into a ring.
Dip the ring in pekmez diluted with water and coat thickly all over in toasted sesame seeds.
Bake at 220 °C for 18 minutes until golden brown.
Serve with white cheese, tomato, cucumber and olives.

title: Peynirli Poğaça (Soft Yoghurt Buns with White Cheese and Parsley)
instructions: Knead the flour, yoghurt, oil, baking powder, half of the egg and a pinch of salt into a soft dough.
Crumble the feta and mix with chopped parsley.
Divide the dough into 3 pieces, flatten, fill with cheese and seal into half moons.
Brush with the remaining egg, sprinkle with sesame and nigella seeds and bake at 190 °C for 20 minutes until golden brown.

title: Yumurtalı Ekmek (Savoury Egg Bread with White Cheese, Tomato and Cucumber)
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pul biber.
Halve the bread slices and soak them on both sides in the mixture.
Fry in the hot oil for 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Sprinkle with crumbled white cheese and parsley and serve with tomatoes and cucumber.

title: Tahin-Pekmez (Sesame Paste with Grape Molasses) on Wholegrain Bread with Banana and Walnuts
instructions: Stir the tahini and pekmez in a small bowl into a glossy, creamy mixture.
Toast the bread if you like and spread thickly with the cream.
Top with banana slices and chopped walnuts.

title: Yumurtalı Patates (Potato and Pepper Skillet with Eggs)
instructions: Cut the potatoes into small cubes and fry in the oil in a non-stick pan, covered, for 12 minutes, turning occasionally.
Add the spring onions and pepper, fry for 4 minutes and season with salt and pul biber.
Make two hollows, slide the eggs in and let them set, covered, for 4 minutes.
Sprinkle with crumbled beyaz peynir, parsley and dill and serve.

title: Ezogelin Çorbası (Red Lentil Soup with Bulgur, Rice and Mint)
instructions: Dice the onion, sweat in the oil for 4 minutes and briefly toast the tomato and pepper pastes.
Add the washed lentils, bulgur, rice and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until everything is soft.
Season with dried mint, pul biber and salt and blend roughly if you like.
Serve with lemon juice and bread.

title: Yayla Çorbası (Yoghurt and Rice Soup with Mint Butter)
instructions: Cook the rice in the stock for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the yoghurt with the egg yolk and flour until smooth and gradually temper with two ladles of hot stock.
Pour the mixture into the soup while stirring constantly and simmer gently for 5 minutes without letting it bubble.
Melt the butter, let the mint foam up briefly in it, drizzle over the soup and serve with bread.

title: Tarhana Çorbası (Spiced Tarhana Soup) with Yoghurt
instructions: Stir the tarhana into 100 ml cold stock until smooth and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Heat the butter and toast the garlic, tomato paste and pepper paste in it for 1 minute.
Stir in the remaining stock and the tarhana and simmer for 10 minutes while stirring until the soup is creamy.
Sprinkle with mint and serve with yoghurt and bread.

title: Tutmaç Çorbası (Lentil Noodle Soup with Yoghurt and Mint Butter)
instructions: Pre-cook the lentils in the stock for 20 minutes.
Sweat the onion in half of the butter, briefly toast the tomato paste and add to the lentils with the noodles, then cook for another 8 minutes.
Stir the yoghurt with the flour until smooth, temper with a little hot soup and stir in, then let it steep gently for 3 minutes.
Foam the remaining butter with the mint and drizzle over the soup.

title: Kabak Çorbası (Cream of Courgette Soup with Yoghurt, Mint and Pumpkin Seeds)
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat in the oil for 3 minutes.
Dice the courgette and potato, add, top up with stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth and season with salt, pepper and mint.
Serve with a dollop of yoghurt, toasted pumpkin seeds and bread.

title: Karalahana Çorbası (Black Sea Black Cabbage Soup with Beans and Sweetcorn)
instructions: Strip the cabbage from the stalks and cut into fine strips.
Sweat the onion in the oil for 3 minutes and briefly toast the tomato paste.
Add the cabbage, beans, sweetcorn and stock and simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal with a little cold water, stir in and simmer for another 5 minutes until the soup thickens slightly; season with pul biber and salt.

title: Kısır (Bulgur Salad with Pepper Paste, Parsley and Pomegranate Molasses)
instructions: Pour 100 ml hot water over the bulgur, cover and leave to swell for 15 minutes.
Knead the tomato and pepper pastes, oil, pomegranate molasses and lemon juice into the warm bulgur until it is evenly red.
Finely chop the spring onions, parsley, mint, tomato and cucumber, fold in and season with salt and pul biber.
Serve in lettuce leaves.

title: Cacık (Chilled Yoghurt and Cucumber Meze with Dill and Mint) with Wholegrain Pitta
instructions: Peel the cucumber, dice finely and salt lightly.
Stir the yoghurt with grated garlic and cold water until smooth and fold in the cucumber and dill.
Sprinkle with dried mint, drizzle with olive oil and serve well chilled with pitta.

title: Acılı Ezme (Spicy Tomato and Pepper Meze with Walnuts) and Wholegrain Pitta
instructions: Deseed the tomatoes and chop very finely with the pepper, onion and parsley using a large knife.
Finely chop the walnuts and stir in with the pepper paste, pomegranate molasses, oil, lemon juice, pul biber and sumac.
Leave to infuse for 10 minutes and serve with pitta.

title: Piyaz (White Bean Salad with Onions, Egg and Tahini-Lemon Dressing)
instructions: Rinse and drain the beans. Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes and quarter it.
Stir the tahini with the lemon juice, oil, 2 tbsp water and salt into a creamy dressing.
Slice the onion into rings and mix with sumac, dice the tomato.
Mix the beans with the dressing, onions, tomato and parsley and top with the egg.

title: Semizotu Salatası (Purslane with Garlic Yoghurt and Walnuts)
instructions: Wash the purslane, remove thick stalks and chop roughly.
Stir the yoghurt with grated garlic and salt until smooth.
Fold in the purslane, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.
Serve with pitta.

title: Havuç Tarator (Carrot, Yoghurt and Walnut Dip) with Vegetable Sticks
instructions: Coarsely grate the carrots, sweat in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft and leave to cool.
Stir the yoghurt with grated garlic, salt and chopped dill.
Fold in the carrots and half of the chopped walnuts and sprinkle with the remaining walnuts.
Serve with cucumber and pepper sticks.

title: Mercimekli Erişte (Ribbon Noodles with Green Lentils and Crispy Onions)
instructions: Cook the lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until al dente, adding the noodles for the last 8 minutes, then drain.
Slice the onion into half rings and fry in the oil for 8 minutes until golden brown.
